items.title: Pakistan joins Saudi Arabia, Turkiye in ‘all for one’ pact
items.description: • MBS, Shehbaz, Erdogan sign Makkah Joint Defence Agreement to boost ‘collective deterrence against any aggression’ • PM hopes accord will serve as ‘shield of peace’; Erdogan says alliance is open to other friendly nations • Saudi minister insists new bloc no threat to ‘any country’ ISLAMABAD: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in the holy city of Makkah, which empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace. The signing of the agreement was announced by three countries through a joint statement, which was published by Pakis­tan’s Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency. It said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”. “The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.” It also “provides for the enha­ncement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added. The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”. During the Makkah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted. From Pakistan’s side, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony. The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well. Following the formal signing of the pact, photos released by Saudi media showed the world leaders offering prayers at the Al-Safa Palace, overlooking the Holy Ka’aba. ‘Shield of peace’ PM Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security. In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president. He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement. Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries. He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity. Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”. “Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X. He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”. The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”. ‘Open to other nations’ Turkish President Erdogan also reiterated this sentiment, saying that the pact targets no country and remains open to participation of other friendly nations seeking peace, prosperity and stability in the region. In a post on the Turkish social platform NSosyal, Erdogan said on Friday the agreement, based on the principle of collective deterrence, would strengthen security and defence cooperation, joint defence industry projects and counterterrorism efforts. He said the agreement also reaffirms the right to self-defence as defined under Article 51 of the UN Charter. “The agreement does not target any country and is open to the participation of all brotherly countries seeking peace, prosperity and stability in our region,” Erdogan said. Türkiye, he added, would firmly maintain its principled stance in favour of resolving conflicts and crises through dialogue and diplomacy, based on respect for international law and in line with its vision of regional ownership. Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

items.title: KP amends controversial law on lawmakers’ privileges
items.description: • Provisions for lifetime blue passport scrapped; number of lifetime arms licences for MPAs reduced to four • Assembly resolves to resist ‘proposed takeover’ of Hazara areas by federal government PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Assembly on Friday withdrew controversial provisions from the recently enacted KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act, 2026 , including the issuance of official passports to lawmakers and their spouses for life. The provincial assembly had earlier in April passed the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Imm­unities and Privileges) Act, 2026, granting blue passports to members and their spouses, arms licences, blanket immunity from preventive detention, and making the speaker’s permission mandatory before arresting members on criminal charges. However, the law faced harsh criticism from the media and the general public, prompting KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to order a review of the legislation last week. KP Information Minister Shafi Jan also announced that the government would withdraw the controversial clauses and restore the law in accordance with the 1988 Act. According to the amendment tabled by treasury lawmaker Ghazi Ikram during a sitting chaired by KP Assembly Speaker Baber Saleem Swati, the house passed the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Amendment Act, 2026. The controversial provisions were withdrawn, and official passports will now remain valid only for the parliamentary tenure of lawmakers, in accordance with federal law. Also, the number of lifetime non-prohibited bore arms licences was also reduced from eight to four. The concerns raised by the journalist community over enhanced fines and punishments were also addressed, with both fines and punishments being reduced. Territorial integrity The house also unanimously passed a resolution over the possible alteration of the territorial jurisdiction of KP by annexing some parts of the province to the federal territory. The resolution, moved by treasury lawmaker Akbar Ayub, stated that Haripur, Abbottabad and all other districts were integral parts of KP and could not be annexed to any other part of the country. It added that any changes — whether administrative, political, financial or aimed at controlling natural resources — would be against the law. It stated that the residents of the province had constitutional rights over KP’s minerals, forests, hydel projects and other natural resources, and that any direct or indirect attempt to take control of these resources was unacceptable. The resolution stated that any changes to the province’s geographical boundaries for personal interests or political objectives would violate the Constitution and could harm the federation. It strongly condemned any such plan and demanded that the federal government reject such suggestions and respect KP’s geographical, constitutional and administrative status. The resolution added that the provincial assembly, the elected government and the people of KP would take all democratic and peaceful steps to safeguard the province’s geographical sovereignty, constitutional rights, provincial autonomy and natural resources, and would never hesitate to make any sacrifice. The house appealed to all political parties, the legal fraternity, public representatives, civil society, youth and the media to make a joint effort to protect the province’s geographical boundaries and the constitutional rights of its residents. “This house warns the federal government to refrain from making any geographical changes, as such a step will never be acceptable to the people of KP and could harm inter-provincial harmony and national unity,” the resolution read, demanding that the federal government publicly reject any such proposal. Source of revenue During the sitting, MPA Fazal Ilahi said that annexing parts of KP was a conspiracy and was unacceptable, adding that the province generated significant revenue from those areas. Earlier, treasury MPA Sultan-e-Rom informed the house that militancy had returned to Swat district after several years of relative peace. He questioned how long the people would continue to tolerate bombings. He said militants began reappearing in 2022, but massive public protests against their presence helped restore relative normalcy. However, he added that explosions continued to occur across KP and recalled the bloodshed in Swat. “We would rather accept death than face displacement again,” he said. Prescriptions In her call-attention notice, opposition lawmaker Meher Sultana of the PPP informed the house that there was no law requiring doctors to prescribe medicines by their generic names rather than by brand names. She said handwritten prescriptions were often illegible, placing an unnecessary financial burden on patients. She urged the health department to enact legislation requiring doctors to prescribe medicines by their generic names instead of brand names. Health Minister Khal­eequr Rehman informed the house that the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the federal government because the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) registered medicines under brand names. He said there was currently no policy requiring prescriptions by generic name but acknowledged that the issue was open to debate. However, he also argued that prescribing generic names could give medical store owners greater discretion to dispense medicines of their own choice. Opposition lawmaker Shahida Waheed of the ANP informed the house that Mardan Medical Complex catered to patients from Mardan and several other districts, but its CT scan and MRI machines had remained out of order, causing immense hardship for patients. Mr Zaman said the issue had been highlighted on social media and that notice had been taken. He said the CT scan machine was now functional and that the MRI machine would also be made operational soon. The sitting was later adjourned until 2pm on Monday. Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

items.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.20, high-speed diesel by Rs1.50
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Friday reduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.20 and Rs1.50 per litre, respectively. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs327.62 per litre while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will apply from August 8 to 10. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Efforts underway to end deadlock over judges’ appointments
items.description: • Govt’s legal team set to meet Presidency officials as summary remains pending with Zardari • Officials say matter now sub judice after petition filed in IHC ISLAMABAD: In a last-ditch effort to break the deadlock over judicial appointments, the government’s legal team has scheduled a meeting with its counterparts at the Presidency on Sunday, as authorities explore the possibility of unilaterally notifying the confirmation and appointment of high court judges. The development comes as the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has yet to issue its ruling on the maintainability of a petition challenging President Asif Ali Zardari’s alleged failure to assent to the recommendations of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan. The JCP, during its meetings on July 20 and 21, recommended the confirmation of four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court, a six-month extension for an additional judge of the Sindh High Court, and the appointment of 19 additional judges to the Lahore, Islamabad, Sindh and Balochistan high courts. Under Clause 8 of Article 175-A of the Cons­titution, the recommendations were forwarded to the prime minister, who then sent the summary to the president. However, the summary has remained pending with the president since then. Amid the stalemate, the government is examining the possibility of invoking Article 48(1) of the Constitution to issue the notifications through the law ministry, arguing that the president was required to act on the summary within a fortnight of its submission — a period that has since expired. However, government functionaries have maintained that with the matter now sub judice, notifications cannot be issued at this stage. Sources said the government’s legal team planned to pursue an “out-of-court” settlement with its counterparts at the Presidency. The president’s legal team has raised certain objections to the JCP proceedings, noting that nearly all nominees proposed by the PPP were rejected. They also conveyed that some candidates recommended for appointment have criminal records. The Presidency’s legal team contends that Article 175-A does not prescribe a specific timeframe for the president’s action and that the provision cannot be overridden by Article 48(1) to bypass the Presidency. They have also referred to Article 48(2), which empowers the president “to act in his discretion in respect of any matter in respect of which he is empowered by the Constitution to do so” and states that validity of anything done by the president shall not be called into question on any ground whatsoever. Sources in the Presidency cautioned that any unilateral action in such a sensitive matter would be a “political and legal disaster”. According to them, the only way forward is to reach a consensus through democratic means. They warned that bypassing the prescribed procedure could trigger significant complications and suggested that any ambiguity regarding Articles 48(1), 48(2) and 175-A(8) should be resolved through mutual consultation between the president and the prime minister rather than through unilateral action. On the other hand, government sources maintained that judicial appointments were governed by constitutional provisions and that any deadlock must be resolved strictly in accordance with the Constitution. Meanwhile, the IHC has reserved its verdict on the maintainability of a petition filed by advocate Luqman Chaudhary through his counsel Zahid Chaudhry, seeking a direction to the president to approve the summary. During Thursday’s hearing, Justice Arbab Muh­ammad Tahir questioned how the court could issue directions to the president and reserved his order. It was initially expected that the ruling would be issued the same day, but Justice Arbab left his office without delivering it. The order was then anticipated on Friday morning, but the file had not been returned from the judge’s chamber by the close of business. The delay has already created practical complications. Four additional judges of the PHC, whose confirmations were recommended by the JCP, ceased to hold office after their tenure expired on Aug 4 due to the absence of formal notifications. Similarly, an additional judge of the SHC, whose term was extended by six months, relinquished office after his tenure expired on July 29. Minister of State for Law and Justice Barrister Aqeel Malik said the government would resolve the matter within the constitutional framework and in accordance with the principles laid down by the superior courts. Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

items.title: NDC historiographies unveiled ahead of launch on 28 September at UPSA
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has unveiled a six-volume publication documenting the party’s and the 4th Republic of Ghana’s political history. This is described as a significant step towards preserving its legacy and strengthening institutional memory for future generations. The collection traces the party’s journey from its formation to the present day, capturing key milestones including media coverage of the NDC over the years, leadership elections, manifesto development, constitutional reforms and other defining moments in the party’s evolution. As a prelude to the main launch scheduled for September 28, 2026, at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), copies of the books were formally presented to the National Chairman of the NDC, Mr. Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, and the party. Receiving the books, Mr. Asiedu Nketiah said the project marks only the beginning of a broader effort to ensure the party systematically documents its history and administrative records. “We will move ahead to a point where we will be able to document the minutes of our meetings. When you want to refer to a decision the party has ever taken, you should be able to trace the meeting, the date and the minutes to see exactly how those decisions were made,” he said. He commended the team behind the project for compiling historical records, including the party’s original founding documents submitted to the Electoral Commission during its registration. “We now have correct documentation of how the party was founded, the original founding documents with the original signatures of our founding fathers and our journey from our first election up to today,” he added. Mr Asiedu Nketiah explained that the publication includes a manifesto volume that chronicles the changing priorities of the country through successive election manifestos. “When you read the manifesto scroll closely, it gives you an indication of what the national needs were at the time those manifestos were prepared. It helps people appreciate where the nation has come from,” he explained. He added that another volume documents the evolution of the NDC’s constitution, providing historical context to current debates on internal party governance. Reflecting on the party’s formative years, the National Chairman recounted how parliamentary candidates were initially selected before the introduction of competitive internal primaries, describing how the NDC’s democratic structures have evolved over time. The official launch, according to Oswald Okaitei, a member of the Book Launch Planning Committee, will feature book review discussions featuring notable political figures and academics on selected chapters of the historiographies to stimulate conversations on the party’s history, institutional development and contribution to Ghana’s democratic journey. He also noted that “Beyond serving as a reference for the political heritage of the fourth Republic of Ghana, it is planned that proceeds from the sale of the books will also be used to support cancer treatment and the cardio therapy unit”. The party, through its Chairman, Mr. Asiedu Nketiah, has encouraged both its members and the general public to purchase the books in support of the initiative.

items.title: Building green cities: Experts call for better planning, waste recovery and sustainable financing
items.description: Building green cities is not simply about planting more trees. It requires a deliberate transformation of how cities generate energy, manage waste, finance infrastructure, move people and protect natural resources. That was the consensus among policymakers, sustainability experts and development partners during a high-level dialogue on green urban development, where participants stressed that Ghana must move beyond policy ambitions to practical, bankable projects capable of attracting long-term investment. They argued that while Ghana has developed several policies on climate action, energy transition and urban development, implementation remains slow because of inadequate planning, fragmented institutional coordination and limited financing. Waste segregation & circular economy Senior Sustainability Officer at the Jospong Green Transitions Office, Dr. Gloria Boamah Kusi, said efficient waste segregation at source remains the foundation of any successful circular economy. Speaking at a two-day seminar on the National Urban Policy 2026-2035 & National Slum Upgrading and Preservation Strategy 2026-2035, Dr. Boamah Kusi said building green cities is an arduous task. According to her, waste should no longer be viewed merely as refuse but as a valuable resource capable of generating new products, renewable energy and employment when properly managed. “If we want to harness the value of waste, we must embrace segregation at the point of generation,” she said. She explained that separating waste at source significantly improves material recovery, making recycling and compost production more efficient. She said efficient collection systems should feed Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs), where recyclable materials can be recovered while organic waste is converted into compost for agricultural use. Beyond waste recovery, she noted that truly green cities must integrate renewable energy, sustainable transport systems, climate-responsive infrastructure and adequate green spaces to reduce carbon emissions and improve urban resilience. Green cities require integrated planning Project Manager for Energy Transition and Green Infrastructure at the French Development Agency (AFD) for Ghana and Liberia, Doris Edem Agbevivi, said waste management, transport and energy are interconnected sectors that must be planned together if cities are to become environmentally sustainable. She observed that although Ghana has made progress, waste management remains largely linear, with much of the waste collected ending up at disposal sites instead of being recovered for economic value. “When we simply collect waste and dump it, we have not achieved much,” she said. She noted that apart from initiatives being undertaken by the Jospong Group, many waste collection systems still operate without resource recovery as their primary objective. Mrs. Agbevivi questioned the sustainability of the country’s transition to electric mobility if supporting infrastructure is not equally green. “If we are using electric vehicles, what powers the charging systems? Where will the batteries be recycled?” she asked, stressing that every aspect of the green transition must be considered holistically. She pointed out that even communities that appear environmentally friendly, such as Aburi, still face challenges with waste recycling, demonstrating that green cities require more than aesthetics. The Yale University Climate Fellow said financing remains one of the biggest barriers to sustainable urban development. According to her, Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) provide catalytic, patient capital, but only where governments can present credible, well-developed investment plans. “We do not need plans that simply end as feasibility studies. We need plans that generate implementable projects,” she said. She explained that development partners consistently look for measurable milestones, clear implementation strategies and bankable projects before committing financial support. Waste management & climate returns Representing the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Ing. Godfred Fiifi Boadi Esq. observed that countries around the world are pursuing green city agendas, although implementation often differs because of local realities. He noted that Ghana’s Energy Transition Framework already recognises waste management, transport and energy as critical components of national climate action. However, he argued that investment priorities need to shift. According to him, comparatively smaller investments in waste management can deliver greater environmental and economic returns than significantly larger investments in other sectors. “If we evaluate projects based on total life-cycle costs, waste management becomes one of the smartest investments a country can make,” he said. He explained that countries often focus only on the initial cost of infrastructure while ignoring recurring operational and maintenance costs throughout the asset’s lifetime. He also advocated the effective implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), under which manufacturers contribute to the cost of collecting, recycling and safely disposing of products after consumer use. Instead of shifting the financial burden to taxpayers and local assemblies, producers should take greater responsibility for the entire life cycle of their products, he said. Improved Policy Implementation Deputy Director for Environment at the Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology, Raymond Ohene Ofori, said Ghana already possesses several policy frameworks capable of supporting green city development. According to him, what is required now is effective implementation supported by sustainable financing mechanisms. He disclosed that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) now hosts Ghana’s Carbon Market Office, creating opportunities for climate finance to support green projects. “If there is a clear strategy, institutions can help mobilise the necessary resources for implementation,” says Ofori, who is also a professional planner. He explained that existing national strategies already guide sustainable transport, renewable energy, circular waste management and protection of wetlands and marine ecosystems. He stressed that the concept of green cities extends far beyond tree planting and encompasses cleaner transport systems, climate-resilient infrastructure, responsible waste management and sustainable urban planning. Greater institutional coordination needed Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Ahmed Ibrahim, called for stronger collaboration among government ministries and agencies responsible for urban development. He observed that local assemblies alone cannot deliver green cities because responsibilities relating to roads, housing, transport and sanitation are spread across multiple ministries. According to him, achieving sustainable urban development requires coordinated planning and implementation rather than isolated interventions. He noted that many Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives are often compelled to undertake projects outside their statutory mandates because of institutional overlaps and service delivery gaps. Turning vision into reality The discussion concluded with a shared message: Ghana possesses the policy frameworks, technical expertise and growing private sector capacity needed to build green cities. What remains is the political commitment to integrate planning across sectors, mobilise innovative financing, strengthen public-private partnerships and accelerate investment in circular waste management, renewable energy and sustainable transport. For many participants, waste represents one of the country’s greatest untapped resources. Rather than viewing it as an environmental burden, they argued, Ghana should treat waste as a valuable economic asset capable of generating jobs, clean energy, compost, recycled materials and significant climate benefits. Only through such an integrated approach, they said, can Ghana build truly green, resilient and inclusive cities for future generations. By Adade Gyamfi

items.title: USA : Meta devra verser près d’un milliard de dollars pour "préjudice sur les jeunes"
items.description: Le géant américain Meta a été condamné à verser près d’un milliard de dollars pour les préjudices imputés à ses plateformes sur les jeunes et devra restreindre l’accès des mineurs à certaines fonctionnalités de Facebook et Instagram, une première aux Etats-Unis. Cette condamnation, prononcée pour « trouble à l’ordre public » par un juge du Nouveau-Mexique, s’accompagne de mesures inédites à l’encontre du groupe dirigé par Mark Zuckerberg. Le magistrat a notamment ordonné la création d’un fonds de réparation de 567 millions de dollars par le géant américain, destiné à financer, pendant cinq ans, des programmes de santé mentale et de prévention en faveur des jeunes. Cette somme vient s’ajouter aux 375 millions de dollars d’amendes infligées en mars par le jury d’un tribunal civil de Santa Fe, qui avait estimé que Meta avait failli à son obligation de protéger les utilisateurs mineurs. Le montant total des sanctions prononcées à l’encontre du groupe dans le cadre de cette procédure atteint ainsi 942 millions de dollars, même si la portée du jugement demeure limitée au Nouveau-Mexique. L’ampleur de la facture pourrait toutefois s’accroître pour Meta en cas de décisions similaires dans d’autres procédures engagées à travers le pays. Le groupe doit notamment comparaître dès la semaine prochaine dans le cadre d’un nouveau procès en Californie, alors qu’une trentaine d’États américains ont engagé des poursuites contre l’entreprise. Le procureur général du Nouveau-Mexique, Raul Torrez, a salué « une victoire historique pour les habitants de cet Etat de l'ouest américain et pour les familles dans tout le pays » et « pour chaque parent qui s'est inquiété des effets des réseaux sociaux sur son enfant ». « Cette affaire a toujours consisté à protéger les enfants, à défendre les familles et faire en sorte que l'une des plus grandes entreprises technologiques au monde ne puisse pas tirer profit sans conséquences de pratiques qui mettent en danger les jeunes », a-t-il défendu dans un communiqué. Le juge Bryan Biedscheid a assorti sa décision d'une série de mesures inédites, applicables pendant cinq ans aux comptes des mineurs du Nouveau-Mexique. Elles seront toutefois gelées le temps de la procédure d'appel si Meta verse une caution, et elles ne concernent pas la messagerie WhatsApp. Ces mesures comprennent une limite de 90 heures par mois d'utilisation cumulée de Facebook et Instagram pour les moins de 18 ans. Elles ordonnent aussi de couper certaines notifications aux mineurs entre 22H00 et 07H00, ainsi que pendant les heures de classe durant l'année scolaire, et de leur masquer par défaut les compteurs de « likes ». Parmi les autres obligations figurent l'interdiction pour tout adulte de contacter par message un mineur qui n'est pas dans ses contacts, l'examen par un humain, sous 48 heures, des signalements d'exploitation sexuelle, et la suppression des comptes suspectés d'appartenir à des moins de 13 ans faute de preuve d'âge sous 30 jours. Le juge a toutefois refusé d'autres remèdes réclamés par le procureur, comme la vérification stricte de l'âge à l'inscription, estimant qu'une loi fédérale sur la protection des données des enfants (COPPA) la rendait juridiquement impossible et qu'une telle contrainte imposée à Meta seul pousserait les mineurs vers ses concurrents. Il renonce aussi à interdire le défilement infini (infinite scroll), la lecture automatique des vidéos ou les recommandations algorithmiques, des fonctionnalités très débattues dans les différentes procédures judiciaires menées aux Etats-Unis contre les géants des réseaux sociaux. Le juge a estimé que ces fonctionnalités étaient susceptibles d'être protégées par le premier amendement de la Constitution sur la liberté d'expression, et par une loi américaine sur les télécommunications, qui exonère de responsabilité les plateformes pour les contenus publiés par des utilisateurs. Sur les 567 millions de dollars du fonds de réparation, près des trois quarts (420 millions) sont fléchés vers des soins de santé mentale pour les adolescents, le reste vers le dépistage, la prévention et la coordination des programmes. Meta a fait appel de toutes ces décisions, mais il est dans le collimateur d'une trentaine d'Etats et d'autres procès l'attendent cette année aux Etats-Unis. L'un deux, opposant le groupe de Menlo Park à quatre Etats (Californie, Colorado, Kentucky, New Jersey) doit débuter le 12 août, à Oakland dans la baie de San Francisco. The post USA : Meta devra verser près d’un milliard de dollars pour "préjudice sur les jeunes" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Lebanon says positive progress made in Rome talks with Israel
items.description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said on Friday that progress had been made on border issues and the return of prisoners during the latest negotiations between Lebanon and Israel in Rome. Speaking at a cabinet session, Aoun said the Rome talks addressed four main issues: a ceasefire, the demolition and bulldozing of houses, the border, and the return of prisoners and the identification of pilot areas, according to a statement released by the Lebanese presidency. Aoun said "positive progress" had been made on the border and prisoners' issues, expressing hope that practical steps would emerge soon, the statement said. He said the US administration would work to address the remaining issues of a ceasefire and pilot areas, adding that US General Joseph Clearfield would arrive in Beirut soon to follow up on these matters. Lebanon and Israel have also agreed on a shortlist of countries that could send troops to verify the disarmament of Hezbollah ‌under a US-brokered agreement, with the United States due to pick countries from the list, Reuters reported on Friday, citing a Lebanese official. Hezbollah is not a party to the agreement ​and has refused to give up its arsenal. The official declined to identify any of the countries on the shortlist or say how many there were. Another Lebanese official and two foreign diplomats have previously told Reuters that Israel and the United ​States had vetoed France. "We have reached a short list of countries. We decided which parties were impossible for each ​and set the potential actors," the Lebanese official said. "The Americans will now decide, and could pick more than one country." Israeli and Lebanese officials have finished three days of negotiations in Rome aimed at advancing security arrangements along their border and implementing a framework agreement reached in Washington in late June, local media reported. The talks, opposed by Hezbollah, are the seventh round of negotiations between the two governments. (With input from agencies)

items.title: How Asante Kwaku Berko allegedly paid over $1 million in bribes to former minister, MPs, and gov’t officials to secure deal for Turkish client
items.description: Former Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) Managing Director Asante Kwaku Berko allegedly used more than US$1 million in bribes to Ghanaian government officials, including a former Minister of Power and MPs, to help secure a lucrative power project for his Turkish client, Aksa Enerji Uretim A.S., a United States federal court has heard. Berko, a dual citizen of Ghana and the United States and a former Executive Director in the Investment Banking Division of Goldman Sachs, was convicted by a federal jury in Brooklyn on all counts relating to a corruption scheme involving the development and financing of a power plant in Ghana. The nine-day trial before United States District Judge Diane Gujarati established that Berko and his co-conspirators sought to influence officials at different levels of government to ensure that Aksa, a Turkish energy company and Goldman Sachs client, won the contract to construct and operate the power plant. Berko faces up to 30 years in prison when sentenced and has been remanded pending sentencing. $1m for Minister According to evidence presented at the trial, Berko’s involvement in the deal began in December 2014, at a time when Ghana was grappling with a national energy crisis. As part of efforts to secure the necessary government approvals, Berko and his associates discussed in April 2015 the alleged payment of US$1 million to the Ghanaian Minister of Power responsible for key approvals for the project at the time. A further US$250,000 was allegedly earmarked for the Minister’s senior adviser. The bribery scheme extended beyond the Executive arm of government. After Parliament ratified the Aksa-Ghana power agreement in July 2015, Berko and his co-conspirators exchanged emails detailing further payments. In August 2015, they discussed alleged US$250,000 in bribes to various individuals, including US$46,000 for Members of the Ghanaian Parliament who had participated in the ratification of the agreement. The US prosecutors said Berko personally made the US$46,000 payment. The conspirators also used coded language to discuss the payments. In one exchange, a recipient was said to be waiting for the “holy rain”, a reference to the bribe, and “would appreciate it sooner rather than later”. Officials flown to Turkey The corruption scheme also allegedly involved an all-expenses-paid trip to Turkey for five Ghanaian officials to inspect equipment connected to the proposed power plant. The trip formed part of the broader efforts by Berko and his associates to cultivate support for the project among officials who could influence its approval and implementation. The power plant was projected to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in profits, according to the United States Department of Justice. Scheme concealed Prosecutors said Berko took deliberate steps to conceal the payments from Goldman Sachs and its compliance team, which was responsible for reviewing the transaction. He allegedly lied to the bank’s compliance personnel about aspects of the deal and used his personal email account, rather than his Goldman Sachs business account, to communicate with co-conspirators about the project and the bribes. He also instructed others involved in the scheme to use similar methods. The bribes were allegedly disguised and moved through shell companies, sham invoices, nominee account holders and cash withdrawals, with transactions passing through both US and foreign bank accounts. Goldman Sachs eventually withdrew from the transaction because of corruption concerns. US prosecutors condemn conduct US Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, Joseph Nocella Jr., said the conviction demonstrated the determination of his office to combat international corruption. “Today’s verdict marks another significant victory in this Office’s longstanding commitment to rooting out corruption,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “The defendant abused his access to high-level foreign government officials and his platform as an investment banker at a prestigious American firm to line his own pockets with millions of dollars.” Assistant Attorney General of the US Department of Justice’s Criminal Division, A. Tysen Duva, said the scheme undermined fair competition. “We live in a global economy that American companies must be able to compete in fairly,” said Assistant Attorney General Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “This defendant corrupted that fair competition. He abused his position at a world-renowned American investment bank by helping bribe Ghanaian officials, so he and his co-conspirators, including senior executives at a Turkish company, could make money. Today’s conviction makes clear that criminals who undermine our country’s interests by corrupting foreign governments and cutting off fair competition will face the full force of the Department of Justice.” FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle Jr. also highlighted the role of international cooperation in bringing Berko to justice. “Today’s verdict highlights the importance of domestic and international partnerships, and the magnitude of success that working together creates. The FBI is thankful for the assistance from the Department of Justice and the United Kingdom – specifically to the Office of International Affairs, U.S. Marshals Service, and INTERPOL – in pursuing justice to protect our country’s financial integrity,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle. The US authorities said the United Kingdom, including its National Centre Bureau for INTERPOL, the US Embassy in London, the Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs and the US Marshals Service, provided substantial assistance in securing Berko’s arrest and extradition.

items.title: South African clothing factories struggle after migrant workers flee
items.description: Weeks after xenophobic protests drove thousands of migrant workers from South ​Africa, rows of sewing machines stood idle at a clothing factory in Newcastle, a manufacturing hub in the eastern province of KwaZulu-Natal. The campaign ‌led by anti-immigrant group March and March sought to free up jobs for South Africans, a third of whom are unemployed . But local manufacturers have struggled to fill vacancies left by foreign workers. Reuters visited three factories in late July whose owners said they had lost between 12% and 19% of their workforce during the protests. Some workers had sewing skills in short supply, the owners ​said, while few locals were willing to take the low-paying jobs. “People don’t want to work in factories,” said Mpho Nkosi, a 29-year-old South African administrator ​at one of the firms. Migrants typically work in sectors unappealing to locals, analysts say. It is unclear how widespread current labour ⁠shortages may be, but there have also been reports of unfilled jobs in sugarcane fields. A spokesperson for the Department of Employment and Labour said he was unaware of worker ​shortages and advised employers to seek the department’s assistance with recruitment. SKILLS GAP DISPUTED Months of anti-immigrant marches and vigilante attacks culminated in a June 30 deadline declared by March and ​March for undocumented migrants to leave, prompting many to flee . The group claims immigrants are to blame for South Africa’s economic woes, particularly high unemployment, although researchers dispute this . It argues that employers prefer foreigners who accept lower wages. Factory owners counter that they mostly employ South Africans, while some skilled workers from neighbouring Eswatini and Lesotho are needed for their experience in the garment sector. “We can’t immediately replace ​these skills with locals,” said Alex Liu, a Newcastle factory owner. Another factory owner, Ronghua Yan, started a training course for seven local employees after losing about 40 foreign ​workers in June. Financial constraints do not allow him to train more, he said. The Southern African Clothing and Textile Workers’ Union estimates that 15% of Newcastle’s 15,000-strong textile workforce left during ‌the protests. Union ⁠representative Siyabonga Ntombela disputed the idea of a skills shortage and said the jobs were not being filled because the pay was too low for South Africans. “We have plenty of qualified machinists in South Africa,” he said, adding that commuting costs also deterred South African workers, while at some factories migrant workers lived on site. Labour market researcher Siphelele Ngidi said attracting South Africans to manufacturing jobs would require a government push to revitalise the sector. “It’s not just the wage alone, it’s also the working ​conditions and the possibility of upward mobility,” ​he said. LOW WAGES, FEWER ORDERS Most of ⁠Newcastle’s garment factories are owned by Chinese nationals who have been in South Africa for decades. They produce clothing for domestic retailers in an industry the government has championed to reduce reliance on imports and that is vital to Newcastle’s economy. But workers are ​typically paid per piece completed, meaning only the most productive might earn the national minimum wage of 30.23 rand ($1.83) per ​hour. Many earn less. Factory ⁠owners told Reuters they could not afford to raise wages because retailers pay little for their garments. A pair of jeans starts at 11.50 rand, while a T-shirt can fetch less than half that. The industry suffered a setback in February when government inspections discovered illegal labour practices at some factories. Liu said most factories had lost retail orders as a result, stressing that ⁠not all ​were equally guilty. While that has reduced the urgency of replacing workers who left, the combined impact ​could push some factories over the edge, causing more South Africans to lose jobs than gain them, he said. Liu said his business is operating at a loss and he plans to reassess by December ​whether to shut down. “At the moment everybody’s wait-and-see. I think there’s a possibility we will see a lot of closures in the coming months.” ($1 = 16.4989 rand)

items.title: 2028 presidential talk ‘a betrayal of the cause’ — Vice President shuts down NDC flagbearer discussions
items.description: Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has declined to be drawn into speculation about a possible bid for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential nomination ahead of the 2028 general election, insisting that the immediate priority of the government must be the delivery of its electoral mandate. Responding to a direct question from the host, KSM, on the latest edition of The KSM Show about whether she would consider contesting the NDC flagbearership, the Vice-President deliberately steered the conversation away from her personal political ambitions and towards the task she said the government had been elected to perform. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang recalled the extensive work that went into preparing the NDC’s 2024 manifesto, saying the process involved years of consultations and contributions from Ghanaians across the country and beyond. The manifesto, titled Resetting Ghana: Jobs, Accountability, Prosperity , became the policy platform on which the party campaigned in the 2024 elections. She said the NDC did not receive the mandate of Ghanaians simply to begin positioning for the next election, but to address the challenges confronting the country. “They didn’t vote for us today to be turning about, going or not going. They said, ‘come and solve the problems’. We have an agenda. What we inherited was a very, very tough situation. We have work to do,” She responded. The Vice-President said any early preoccupation with who would lead the party in 2028 could undermine the purpose for which the government was elected. “And it’s not even time [for NDC flagbearer elections]. I think it’s a betrayal of the cause of the people. And I don’t think it is right,” She stressed. She therefore appealed to members and supporters of the NDC to concentrate on implementing the government’s programme rather than engaging in premature succession discussions. “So please help us to fulfil the dreams of this beautiful country that we know much better, even though it is doing now. Let us focus on getting the job done,” She appealed. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang said the administration’s success should ultimately be judged by the quality of its work and the support it provides to Ghanaians, rather than by speculation about its political future. “And it depends on the quality of support we are giving. If you’re already going left and right and centre and back.” She concluded with a clear statement of her immediate priority, saying: “Keep the focus, full the mission, deliver results.” The Vice-President’s comments come as attention within the NDC increasingly turns towards the question of succession ahead of 2028, when President John Dramani Mahama will be constitutionally barred from seeking another term after his return to office in the 2024 election. Mahama won the 2024 presidential election after campaigning on the promise to reset the country’s economy and governance.

items.title: Les CRI ouvrent leurs portes aux Marocains du Monde du 10 au 13 août
items.description: Le ministère de l’Investissement, de la Convergence et de l’Évaluation des Politiques Publiques (MICEPP), en partenariat avec les Centres Régionaux d’Investissement (CRI) du Royaume, organise du 10 au 13 août 2026 une nouvelle édition de la Semaine de l’investissement dédiée aux Marocains du Monde. Cette initiative, précise le MICEPP dans un communiqué, vise à rapprocher les Marocains du Monde des opportunités d’investissement offertes par les différentes régions du Royaume, tout en leur proposant un accompagnement de proximité pour la préparation, le développement et la réalisation de leurs projets. Elle s’inscrit dans le cadre de la vision royale, qui accorde une place centrale à la mobilisation des compétences, des talents et des investissements des Marocains du Monde dans la dynamique de développement économique, social et territorial du Royaume. Cette édition accompagne également la mise en œuvre de la Charte de l’investissement, qui vise à renforcer l’attractivité des territoires, encourager l’investissement productif, simplifier le parcours des investisseurs et favoriser une répartition équilibrée des investissements à l’échelle nationale. À travers les différents mécanismes de soutien mis en place, notamment le dispositif dédié aux Très Petites, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (TPME), les porteurs de projets bénéficient d’un accompagnement adapté favorisant la création d’activités durables, innovantes et génératrices d’emploi. Durant quatre jours, les CRI accueilleront les Marocains du Monde afin de leur présenter les potentialités économiques des différentes régions et de les accompagner dans l’identification d’opportunités adaptées à leurs projets. Le programme comprendra des rencontres avec les équipes des CRI, des sessions d’information sur les dispositifs d’appui et d’incitation à l’investissement, des présentations d’opportunités sectorielles et territoriales ainsi que des échanges avec les acteurs économiques locaux. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux projets relevant des TPME, avec des informations sur les critères d’éligibilité, les formes de soutien disponibles et les modalités d’accompagnement prévues. Les participants pourront ainsi bénéficier d’un accompagnement personnalisé, mieux comprendre les dispositifs de la Charte de l’investissement et identifier des opportunités concrètes dans les secteurs à fort potentiel. Au-delà de cette manifestation, les Centres Régionaux d’Investissement restent mobilisés tout au long de l’année, au Maroc et depuis les pays de résidence des Marocains du Monde, pour les informer, les orienter et les accompagner à chaque étape de leurs projets d’investissement. À travers cette nouvelle édition, le ministère réaffirme son engagement à renforcer les liens entre les Marocains du Monde et les territoires du Royaume, en valorisant leur expertise, leurs initiatives et leur contribution au développement régional inclusif, durable et créateur d’emplois. The post Les CRI ouvrent leurs portes aux Marocains du Monde du 10 au 13 août appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Senegal court jails three TikTok influencers for insulting the president
items.description: A Senegalese court sentenced three TikTok influencers to serve prison time and pay a fine for ​insulting the president, their lawyer said in a ‌video posted on Facebook, a move that critics said was an assault on free speech in the West African country. The three ​men worked for online communications channel Feenal Digital, ​which produces content that some say favors Senegal’s ⁠ousted Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko, the head of the ​PASTEF party. Sonko recently split from his ally, President Bassirou ​Diomaye Faye, who launched his own party last month. Feenal Digital aims to promote government and private-sector activities, according to its description on Facebook. Mandoumbe ​Diop, known as Lamignou Darou, was sentenced to three ​months in prison without suspension. He appeared to be the most ‌influential ⁠of the three, with over half a million followers on his TikTok channel. His videos often draw tens of thousands of views. Magueye Diaw, known as Oustaz Thiep, and ​Moustapha Ndiaye, ​known as Ndiaye ⁠Touba, were each sentenced to two months without parole, Feenal Digital said on Facebook. Their ​lawyer, Abdy Nar Ndiaye, described their posts ​on ⁠TikTok as comical and said they did not merit criminal prosecution. He said Diaw and Ndiaye were fined 500,000 ⁠CFA ($800). Feenal Digital ​and a government spokesperson did ​not immediately respond to requests for comment.

items.title: This Saturday on Prime Insight: Ministerial reshuffle, democracy debate take centre stage
items.description: The upcoming edition of Prime Insight on Joy Prime will focus on two major issues expected to dominate Ghana’s political conversation: President John Dramani Mahama’s latest ministerial reshuffle and renewed claims of threats to democratic governance. The programme, scheduled for 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on Saturday, August 8, 2026, will be hosted by Blessed Sogah and will feature Solomon Owusu, Director of Communications of the United Party; Julius Kwame Anthony, Press Secretary at the Ministry for the Interior; and Ross Osei Owusu, a member of the NPP Legal Directorate. The first discussion will examine the changes in government, including the movement of Kenneth Gilbert Adjei and Ahmed Ibrahim, alongside the appointment of Mahama Ayariga and Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings to new ministerial responsibilities. The reshuffle comes amid continued scrutiny of the performance of government ministries and the effectiveness of President Mahama’s administration. Kenneth Adjei, who previously headed the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources, has been appointed Defence Minister, a move confirmed by the Presidency on Friday. Mr Adjei had been responsible for key areas, including housing, water resources and infrastructure. His successor and the implications of the changes for government policy delivery are expected to feature prominently in the discussion. The programme will also consider the political calculations behind the changes and whether the reshuffle is intended primarily to improve performance, strengthen political coordination or reposition the government ahead of the next phase of its administration. The second major issue is the NPP’s campaign against what it describes as threats to Ghana’s democratic freedoms, under the theme “Democracy Under Attack’ Demo: A March, A Petition, and What Next?” The discussion follows earlier allegations by NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia that Ghana’s democratic credentials and freedom of expression were under threat. He accused the government of using state security institutions to intimidate political opponents. The NPP has previously staged demonstrations over alleged intimidation, arrests and what party officials described as the weaponisation of state institutions. During one such protest in Sunyani, demonstrators presented a petition calling for an end to what they described as a “culture of silence” and threats to fundamental freedoms. Saturday’s Prime Insight is therefore expected to examine the substance of those allegations, the government’s response and whether the protests and petitions can translate into concrete political or institutional action. The programme will air on Joy Prime (DStv 281, GOtv 124, and Free-to-Air channel 102), with live engagement on @JoyPrimeTV across social media.

items.title: Chaouki dénonce le "discours du découragement" et défend la stratégie de proximité du RNI
items.description: Le président du Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI), Mohamed Chaouki, a appelé à privilégier un débat politique « responsable » , estimant que la principale menace qui pèse aujourd'hui sur la vie politique est « le discours du découragement » , qu'il accuse d'alimenter la défiance et de brouiller le débat public. S'exprimant lors d'une rencontre organisée à Ribat El Kheir, dans la province de Sefrou, le dirigeant du RNI a affirmé que les déplacements de son parti à travers les différentes régions du Royaume ne relevaient pas d'une logique de démonstration politique, mais visaient avant tout à recueillir les attentes des citoyens et à nourrir son projet pour les prochaines années. Selon lui, le programme « Dignité et opportunités pour tous » est le fruit d'une large démarche de consultation menée sur le terrain. Cette approche, a-t-il assuré, permet de mieux cerner les priorités exprimées par les Marocains, qu'il a résumées autour de trois attentes : une économie plus dynamique, des services publics plus performants et davantage d'opportunités d’emploi et d'inclusion. Mohamed Chaouki est également revenu sur le bilan de l'Exécutif, estimant que le gouvernement a engagé plusieurs réformes structurantes au cours de son mandat. Il a notamment cité la généralisation progressive de l'État social et le programme d'aide sociale directe, qui bénéficie, a-t-il rappelé, à près de quatre millions de familles. Le président du RNI a insisté sur la volonté du gouvernement de faire parvenir les effets de ces réformes aux catégories qui en ont le plus besoin. Il a ainsi présenté le soutien social direct comme l'un des principaux volets de la politique sociale engagée par l'Exécutif, estimant que la dignité devait se traduire par des mesures concrètes plutôt que rester un simple thème du discours politique. Le responsable du parti de la colombe a également mis en avant le plaidoyer du RNI en faveur d'un renforcement des ressources financières des collectivités territoriales. Pour lui, une partie essentielle du développement passe par les territoires et les communes, qui doivent disposer de moyens suffisants pour améliorer les services fournis quotidiennement aux citoyens. Sur ce point, Mohamed Chaouki a affirmé que son parti continuait à défendre, au sein des institutions, une augmentation des ressources destinées aux collectivités territoriales, considérant que le développement local ne peut être pleinement assuré sans renforcer les capacités financières des communes. En conclusion, Mohamed Chaouki a estimé que le Maroc poursuit une trajectoire de consolidation économique et sociale malgré un contexte international marqué par de nombreuses incertitudes. Il a en ce sens appelé à opposer « un discours d'espoir et d'action » aux discours qu'il juge porteurs de pessimisme, affirmant que le RNI entend poursuivre son action en s'appuyant sur son bilan et sur les échanges menés avec les citoyens. items.title: Manni : le bas-fond qui nourrit l’espoir de tout un village
items.description: Manni : le bas-fond qui nourrit l'espoir de tout un village Manni, 6 août 2026 (AIB)-Au cœur de la commune de Manni, dans la province de la Gnagna, un bas-fond aménagé de 14 hectares, exploité depuis 1978, continue de faire vivre et d'entretenir l'espoir de dizaines de familles. Situé au côté est du pont de Manni, à la sortie nord en direction de Taparko, entre le marché et le quartier Tiamgnalgou, ce périmètre irrigué accueille chaque jour près d'une centaine de producteurs qui s'y activent malgré un début de saison agricole marqué par une pluviométrie tardive et irrégulière, convaincus que la terre demeure l'un des meilleurs remparts contre la faim, la pauvreté et la précarité. Sur les parcelles verdoyantes, les jeunes plants de riz, actuellement au stade du tallage, offrent un spectacle rassurant et laissent entrevoir une campagne prometteuse, à condition que les conditions climatiques restent favorables jusqu'à la récolte. Avant l'installation de cette culture, les exploitants avaient mis à profit la contre-saison pour produire principalement du maïs et de la patate douce, avant de préparer les pépinières puis de procéder au repiquage des jeunes plants de riz, en fonction des besoins de chaque exploitation et des opportunités du marché. Véritable moteur de développement local, ce bas-fond dépasse largement sa vocation agricole. Il constitue un important levier économique et social pour la commune de Manni, en assurant une disponibilité régulière de produits vivriers, en générant des revenus pour les ménages et en renforçant la résilience des populations face aux effets conjugués des changements climatiques et de l'insécurité. Rencontré sur le site, le président du périmètre irrigué, Emmanuel Lankoandé, s'est réjoui de la forte mobilisation des producteurs. « Ce bas-fond nourrit de nombreuses familles. Pour plusieurs exploitants, il représente la principale source de revenus. Il permet de produire, de vendre les récoltes, de couvrir les dépenses familiales et de répondre aux besoins essentiels », a-t-il expliqué. Il a salué les efforts du gouvernement burkinabè en faveur du monde rural, notamment à travers la mise à disposition de semences améliorées, d'intrants agricoles ainsi que l'accompagnement à la commercialisation des productions. Il a également exprimé sa reconnaissance envers les organisations non gouvernementales dont l'appui en équipements, notamment l'acquisition d'un motoculteur, facilite considérablement les travaux agricoles tout en réduisant la pénibilité du labour. Le président du périmètre a aussi rendu hommage au technicien agricole qui accompagne les producteurs tout au long de la campagne. Ses conseils, allant du choix des variétés à la gestion de l'eau d'irrigation, en passant par la fertilisation des sols et la lutte contre les maladies et les ravageurs, contribuent significativement à l'amélioration des rendements. Malgré ces acquis, Emmanuel Lankoandé nourrit une ambition majeure : le désensablement du barrage qui alimente le périmètre irrigué. Selon lui, cette opération permettrait d'accroître la capacité de rétention d'eau, d'étendre les superficies aménagées et d'offrir des parcelles à un plus grand nombre de producteurs. Parmi les exploitants figure Haro Talata, venu de Boungou-Folgou. Reconnaissant envers les propriétaires terriens qui lui ont cédé une portion de terre, il mesure l'importance de cet élan de solidarité. « Sans cette solidarité, je n'aurais pas pu produire ici. Aujourd'hui, je nourris l'espoir de réaliser une bonne récolte », a-t-il confié avec optimisme. Même satisfaction chez Bourgou Moussa, qui fréquente le site depuis une vingtaine d'années. « Grâce à cette exploitation, j'arrive à nourrir ma famille, à assurer les dépenses du ménage et à scolariser mes enfants », a-t-il témoigné, soulignant l'impact durable du périmètre sur les conditions de vie de nombreux ménages. En dépit d'une installation tardive et irrégulière des pluies cette année, les producteurs poursuivent avec détermination les travaux d'entretien des parcelles, convaincus que leurs efforts seront récompensés. Leur engagement s'inscrit dans l'appel lancé par le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, à produire et consommer local afin de renforcer la souveraineté alimentaire du Burkina Faso. Dans cette partie de la Gnagna, où les défis sécuritaires et climatiques demeurent, le bas-fond de Manni apparaît comme bien plus qu'un simple espace de production. Il est le symbole d'une agriculture résiliente, portée par le courage des producteurs, la solidarité communautaire et l'espoir d'un avenir meilleur. Chaque campagne agricole y rappelle que, malgré les difficultés, la terre continue d'offrir des perspectives à ceux qui la cultivent avec persévérance. Agence d'information du Burkina GL/oat/ata

items.title: Kadiogo/Koubri : les populations mobilisées pour le désherbage du champ du chef de canton
items.description: Kadiogo/Koubri : les populations mobilisées pour le désherbage du champ du chef de canton Koubri, 5 août 2026 (AIB)-Les populations de Koubri se sont fortement mobilisées, mercredi, pour les travaux de désherbage et de sarclage du champ de sorgho rouge de Sa Majesté le Naaba Kangré, chef de canton de Koubri, perpétuant ainsi une tradition de solidarité, d'entraide et d'engagement communautaire. Fidèles à une coutume bien établie, les habitants de toutes les couches sociales se retrouvent chaque année, à la période de montaison des cultures, dans le champ du chef de canton pour effectuer les opérations culturales. Dès les premières heures de la matinée, hommes, femmes, jeunes et personnes âgées ont pris d'assaut le champ de l'autorité coutumière, témoignant de leur attachement aux valeurs traditionnelles et de leur respect envers le garant des us et coutumes du canton. Au-delà de son caractère coutumier, cette mobilisation constitue un cadre privilégié de renforcement de l'unité, de la solidarité et du vivre-ensemble. Elle contribue à consolider la cohésion sociale et à préserver les liens de fraternité entre les différentes composantes de la communauté. À cette occasion, Sa Majesté le Naaba Kangré a invité les populations à demeurer attachées aux valeurs endogènes qui fondent l'identité de la nation burkinabè, notamment l'amour de la patrie, l'intégrité, le respect des us et coutumes ainsi que des traditions, tout en les exhortant à œuvrer inlassablement à la préservation de la paix et de la cohésion sociale. À l'issue des travaux, le chef de canton a exprimé sa profonde gratitude aux populations pour leur forte mobilisation et leur disponibilité à répondre, une fois de plus, à son appel. Il s'est également réjoui du bon déroulement des opérations de désherbage, réalisées dans un climat de solidarité et de parfaite entente. Selon Sa Majesté, cette mobilisation dépasse le simple cadre des travaux champêtres. « Ces retrouvailles constituent un moment privilégié de rapprochement, de fraternisation et de consolidation de la cohésion sociale », a-t-il déclaré, avant d'inviter les filles et fils du canton à préserver cet esprit d'unité, gage d'une paix durable et d'un développement harmonieux de la commune. Agence d'information du Burkina LZ/C-AIB Koubri

items.title: Situation sécuritaire dans l’AES : La Confédération des États du Sahel regrettent les propos du président nigérian
items.description: Le Ministre des Affaires étrangères, le Camarade Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ, a reçu, dans la soirée du jeudi 06 août 2026, le Chargé d’Affaires de l’Ambassade de la République fédérale du Nigéria au Burkina Faso, à la suite des déclarations du Président nigérian, Bola Ahmed TINUBU, sur la situation sécuritaire dans les pays de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). Cette rencontre s’est déroulée en présence des Chargés d’Affaires des Ambassades du Mali et du Niger, illustrant la position concertée et solidaire des trois États membres de la Confédération. Le 30 juillet dernier, lors d’une rencontre avec des chefs traditionnels nigérians, le Président TINUBU a imputé la recrudescence des enlèvements et des attaques terroristes au Nigéria à ce qu’il a qualifié d’« effondrement » de la sécurité dans les pays voisins du Sahel. « Certains d’entre eux (les terroristes) ne sont pas Nigérians. Vous voyez, le problème de l’insécurité au Mali, au Burkina Faso et au Niger ne fait qu’aggraver nos difficultés. », avait affirmé le Président TINUBU devant les chefs traditionnels nigérians. Au nom de ses homologues du Mali et du Niger, le Ministre Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ a exprimé le profond regret des pays de la Confédération face à ces propos inexacts et peu compatibles avec l’esprit de solidarité qui doit prévaloir entre États voisins confrontés à une menace commune. Selon le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè, cette lecture de la situation sécuritaire occulte les sacrifices considérables consentis quotidiennement par les Forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi que par les populations, du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger dans la lutte contre le terrorisme. « C’est une analyse rapide, très simpliste et surprenante, qui révèle un biais préoccupant de la part de la première autorité du Nigéria. Nous aurions souhaité que le contexte sécuritaire soit présenté avec davantage de justesse, plutôt que de faire porter à des pays voisins la responsabilité d’une situation complexe, au risque d’alimenter des incompréhensions et des frustrations entre des peuples liés par l’histoire, la géographie et la fraternité », a déclaré le Ministre TRAORÉ. Pour le cas particulier du Niger, le ministre des Affaires étrangères estime que les propos du Président TINUBU constituent un mépris du sacrifice consenti par l’armée nigérienne face à Boko Haram depuis des années, alors que le phénomène de terrorisme ne sévissait pas encore dans les pays de la Confédération AES. Le Ministre a par ailleurs rappelé que malgré les connexions établies entre Boko Haram et certains groupes terroristes actifs au Sahel, les États de la Confédération AES se sont toujours gardés de toute accusation publique contre le Nigéria, privilégiant une approche fondée sur la coopération et la responsabilité partagée. Pour le Chef de la diplomatie burkinabè, « le Burkina Faso, le Mali, le Niger et le Nigéria font face au même ennemi. À ce titre, les succès enregistrés par les Forces de défense et de sécurité des pays de l’AES bénéficient à la sécurité de l’ensemble de la sous-région, y compris du Nigéria, en limitant les capacités de nuisance et la mobilité des groupes terroristes ». Le Ministre TRAORÉ a ainsi invité les autorités nigérianes à privilégier des discours fédérateurs et porteurs de solidarité, plutôt que des déclarations susceptibles d’alimenter les divisions ou les malentendus entre peuples voisins. « Nous ne sommes pas responsables de ce qui nous arrive. Nous en payons la facture, mais les véritables ennemis sont ailleurs. C’est pourquoi nous devons agir comme des peuples frères, unis par une même histoire et confrontés à une même menace », a-t-il souligné. Le Ministre Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORÉ a réaffirmé que la démarche des trois pays de la Confédération AES ne relevait ni de la polémique ni de la confrontation diplomatique, mais traduisait la volonté d’entretenir un dialogue franc, respectueux et constructif entre États frères, convaincus que seule une coopération sincère permettra de relever durablement les défis sécuritaires de la sous-région. En réponse, le Chargé d’Affaires de l’Ambassade du Nigéria a indiqué avoir pris bonne note du message qui lui a été transmis et s’est engagé à en rendre fidèlement compte à ses autorités à Abuja. Il a, par ailleurs, reconnu les efforts considérables consentis par les pays de la Confédération des États du Sahel dans la lutte contre le terrorisme, citant notamment le rôle déterminant joué par le Niger dans la prévention d’attaques qui auraient pu viser le territoire nigérian. Le diplomate nigérian a enfin salué la démarche des Ministres des Affaires étrangères de la Confédération AES, y voyant la volonté des États voisins de privilégier le dialogue, la compréhension mutuelle et la solidarité face à une menace commune. L’article Situation sécuritaire dans l'AES : La Confédération des États du Sahel regrettent les propos du président nigérian est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Burkina Faso : La centrale thermique Bobo 2 inaugurée pour renforcer la souveraineté énergétique
items.description: Avec une capacité installée de 26,4 MW, la centrale thermique Bobo 2, inaugurée le 7 août 2026, marque une étape clé dans la stratégie de souveraineté énergétique du Burkina Faso. Le Burkina Faso poursuit son ambition d’autonomie énergétique. Ce vendredi 7 août 2026, la ville de Bobo-Dioulasso a accueilli la cérémonie officielle d’inauguration de la centrale thermique Bobo 2, présidée par le ministre de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, sous le haut patronage du Premier ministre Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo. D'une capacité installée de 26,4 MW, le coût total de l'investissement est etsimé à plus de 33 milliards FCFA et entierrement financé par la SONABEL Cette infrastructure énergétique s’inscrit dans la dynamique enclenchée par le gouvernement, après l’inauguration de la centrale thermique de Pabré, et avant celles prévues à Koudougou et Kaya. Dans son allocution, le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba a souligné que « le Burkina Faso bâtit, pierre après pierre, sa souveraineté énergétique », rappelant que chaque nouvelle centrale contribue à renforcer la sécurité énergétique nationale et à améliorer l’accès à l’électricité pour les populations. L’inauguration de Bobo 2 illustre la volonté du gouvernement de diversifier les sources de production et de consolider les infrastructures énergétiques, afin de soutenir le développement économique et social du pays.
