items.title: 2027: Ortom denies plot to replace Aondoakaa as Benue PDP candidate
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi MAKURDI — Former Benue State Governor and leader of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the state, Chief Samuel Ortom, has dismissed reports alleging that he and other party leaders are planning to replace the party’s 2027 governorship candidate, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, with the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Shippers’ Council, Dr Pius Akutah. Ortom, in a statement issued by his Media Assistant, Zege Terhide, described the report circulating on social media as a “mischievous” distortion of a recent meeting involving prominent Benue stakeholders. The former governor explained that he, alongside the Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, and the PDP governorship candidate, Aondoakaa, met with prominent Benue indigenes, including Chief Simon Shango, Prof Iyorwuese Hagher, Dr Pius Akutah, Emmanuel Ameh and Dr Matthias Byuan. According to him, the meeting was part of ongoing consultations aimed at building a broad strategic alliance among Benue stakeholders in the overall interest of the state. “At no time during the meeting was the replacement of Chief Aondoakaa as the PDP governorship candidate discussed, contemplated or placed on the agenda,” Ortom said. He described attempts to give the meeting a different interpretation as mischievous, stressing that political consultations across party lines were normal in a democratic environment. “It is therefore mischievous for anyone to take a legitimate meeting of Benue leaders and manufacture an entirely different motive for it,” he said. Ortom maintained that consultations and engagements involving political actors and stakeholders should not automatically be interpreted as secret conspiracies, particularly when such engagements were motivated by the larger interest of the people. “Political consultations and engagements across party lines are neither strange nor secret conspiracies, particularly when they are driven by the larger interest of the people,” he stated. The former governor also dismissed speculation over the PDP governorship ticket, declaring that Aondoakaa remained the party’s duly nominated candidate for the 2027 governorship election in the state. “Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, remains the duly nominated governorship candidate of the PDP in Benue State for the 2027 election,” Ortom declared. He said the former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice enjoyed the confidence and support of the PDP leadership and members across the state. Ortom also expressed confidence in Aondoakaa’s ability to provide effective leadership if elected, citing his experience, competence and understanding of the challenges facing Benue. He said Aondoakaa had the capacity to reposition the state and provide purposeful leadership, particularly in the areas of security, economic recovery and sustainable development. The former governor therefore urged those responsible for circulating the alleged replacement story to desist from spreading what he described as fabricated narratives capable of causing confusion within the PDP and among supporters of its governorship candidate. “Political journalism and commentary must be anchored on facts, not conjecture, deliberate falsehood or the attribution of imaginary motives to legitimate engagements,” he cautioned. Ortom urged PDP members, supporters of Aondoakaa and the people of Benue State to disregard the report and remain focused on the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections. He stressed that the alleged misinformation would not distract the PDP leadership from its efforts to build what he described as a formidable coalition of Benue people capable of providing the state with a credible alternative in 2027. items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira appreciated to N1,412 per dollar in the parallel market on Friday, from N1,416 per dollar recorded on Thursday. Similarly, the local currency strengthened to N1,364 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the indicative exchange rate for the naira stood at N1,364 per dollar, compared with N1,365.10 per dollar on Thursday, representing an appreciation of N1.10. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N48 per dollar from N50.90 per dollar recorded on Thursday. items.title: Gender Minister monitors LEAP enrolment exercise in Savelugu, Kumbungu

The visits formed part of the second day of her working tour of the Northern and North East regions, where she was accompanied by members of the Ministry’s Advisory Board to assess the progress of the ongoing enrolment exercise. As part of the engagements, Dr Lartey paid courtesy calls on the Chief of Savelugu, Yoo Naa Abdulai Yakubu, and the Chief of Kumbungu, Gbullung Naa Musah Surani, where she acknowledged the critical role traditional authorities play in supporting social protection programmes within their communities. The Minister also met the Municipal Chief Executive for Savelugu, Alhassan Fuseini, and the District Chief Executive for Kumbungu, Imoro Yakubu Kakpagu, to strengthen collaboration towards the successful implementation of the enrolment exercise. Dr Lartey and her delegation further visited selected LEAP enrolment centres, where they interacted with beneficiaries, prospective applicants and field officers to assess the progress of the exercise and gain first-hand insight into the experiences of participants. She commended the traditional authorities, local government officials and community members for their cooperation and support, noting that their contributions were essential to the success of the programme. The Minister also urged all stakeholders to continue working together to ensure that vulnerable households are successfully enrolled and receive the support provided under the LEAP programme.

items.title: Alaafin: Oyo passport office autonomy’ll boost local economy, ease travel burden
items.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — The Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Owoade, has welcomed the newly granted autonomy to the Oyo Passport Office, describing the development as a significant step towards decentralising government services and stimulating economic activities in the ancient city. The monarch said the development would bring critical government services closer to residents, particularly those in rural and semi-urban communities who previously had to travel to Ibadan or Ilorin to access passport-related services. Oba Owoade stated this through a high-powered delegation led by a member of the Oyo Traditional Council (Oyo Mesi), High Chief Asimiyu Atanda, during a visit to the Oyo Passport Office to felicitate with its management on the autonomy recently granted to the facility. Before the development, the Oyo Passport Office operated as an appendage of the Ibadan Passport Office and was required to refer certain operations to the latter. With the new status, however, the Oyo Passport Office can operate independently, while international passports processed through the facility will bear the name of the Oyo Passport Office. The Alaafin said the development was significant because having a local passport office was essential to decentralising government services and improving accessibility. He noted that the autonomous facility would “eliminate long-distance travel to state capitals” and reduce pressure on major passport processing centres. According to him, residents would no longer have to bear the additional transportation costs and time associated with travelling outside Oyo for biometric capture, documentation and other passport-related services. Oba Owoade said the development would “bring biometric capture and documentation services closer to rural or semi-urban residents, saving travel time and transport costs.” The monarch also linked the development to broader economic benefits for Oyo, arguing that increased movement of applicants and visitors to the city would generate additional patronage for local businesses. He said the office would “alleviate massive workloads and long queues at Central State or Regional Passport Headquarters” while creating opportunities for businesses operating around the facility. “It would also increase local commercial activities as travellers from neighbouring towns visit the city for administrative processing, as well as create jobs directly through facility staffing and indirectly via local micro-businesses that support office visitors,” the Alaafin said. Earlier, the Chief Passport Officer of the Oyo Passport Office, Assistant Controller of Immigration Oladejo Taiwo David, expressed appreciation to the Alaafin and his delegation for the visit. Oladejo acknowledged the role played by the monarch and other prominent Oyo indigenes in securing the autonomous status for the office. “This feat wouldn’t have been achieved if not for the efforts of His Imperial Majesty,” he said, while also acknowledging the support of prominent Oyo sons, particularly Alhaji Daud Igi-Ogun. The Chief Passport Officer appealed to the Alaafin to assist the office in creating awareness among residents about the services now available in Oyo. He urged residents to take advantage of the development by patronising the Oyo Passport Office instead of travelling to Ibadan or Ilorin for passport-related services. “We solicit the support of His Imperial Majesty in the creation of awareness for the people to start patronising the Passport Office instead of going to Ibadan and Ilorin,” Oladejo said. He assured residents that the new autonomous status would lead to more efficient service delivery. According to him, “Oyo Passport Office would serve the people better as it would be faster to get their passports.” The Alaafin’s delegation comprised the Director of Administration to the monarch, Prince Adesola Sanda, and renowned Sheikh, Alhaji Daud Igi-Ogun. The post Alaafin: Oyo passport office autonomy’ll boost local economy, ease travel burden appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ecstasy as Arugba leads Osun procession with sacred votary
items.description: — Adams seeks FG support, new innovations By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo OSOGBO — There was excitement among worshippers and participants at the Osun-Osogbo Festival as the Arugba, Osunbunmi Moradeke, led the annual procession into the Osun Sacred Grove with the sacred votary for the first time since her selection two years ago. Moradeke was selected through the Ifa divination process in 2025 following the retirement of the previous Arugba after she got married. However, Moradeke’s physical condition prevented her from carrying the sacred votary during last year’s festival, with the responsibility instead performed by the Baba Osun. Her appearance at the grove this year with the votary generated excitement among worshippers, who offered prayers and expressed thanksgiving, a major feature of the annual festival. Meanwhile, the Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, represented at the event by his Deputy, Kola Adewusi, reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to preserving the state’s cultural heritage and protecting the Osun Sacred Grove, a globally recognised heritage site. Adewusi said the state government would continue to support indigenous cultural activities capable of promoting Osun State and its heritage to the world. He said, “As we celebrate this sacred tradition, may the blessings of Osun continue to bring peace, prosperity and progress to our dear state. “Our administration’s commitment to preserving Osun’s rich cultural heritage and protecting the Osun Sacred Grove as a globally treasured heritage site remains unwavering.” Also speaking, the Aare Ona Kakanfo of Yorubaland, Iba Gani Adams, called for greater use of technology and digital platforms to expand the global reach and economic impact of the annual Osun-Osogbo Festival. Adams said technology could play a significant role in preserving Yoruba cultural heritage, attracting international audiences and connecting younger generations with the traditions of their ancestors. He said, “First, we must leverage technology to enhance the festival experience. This includes live streaming events to global audiences, developing interactive digital platforms for cultural education, and using social media to engage younger generations worldwide.” He also called for greater involvement of the Federal Government and the introduction of new innovations to strengthen the festival’s global appeal and economic benefits. The post Ecstasy as Arugba leads Osun procession with sacred votary appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Osun Election: APC, Adeleke campaign trade accusations over alleged oath-taking, vote buying
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship campaign council has accused Governor Ademola Adeleke of alleged involvement in oath-taking and vote-buying activities ahead of the August 15 governorship election. The APC campaign council alleged that members of the Accord Party had been administering oaths to residents and allegedly inducing them with money to support Adeleke at the poll. In a statement on Friday, Chairman of the APC Media Committee, Remi Omowaye, said the party had video evidence purportedly showing Accord members distributing money to residents after administering oaths of allegiance. Omowaye described the alleged practice as a dangerous development capable of undermining the democratic process. He said, “This latest dimension of vote-buying is not only dastardly and crude but also morally reprehensible. It represents a dangerous descent into political desperation and an affront to the democratic values that guarantee every citizen the freedom to vote according to their conscience without coercion, intimidation or manipulation.” The APC campaign council further alleged that the development showed that the governor was worried about his chances in the election. The party claimed that the alleged activities were aimed at influencing vulnerable citizens, adding that political campaigns should be based on achievements and policies rather than coercion. However, the Imole Campaign Council Media Committee Chairman, Bamidele Salam, dismissed the allegations, saying Governor Adeleke was not involved in or aware of any such activities. Salam said the council was investigating the authenticity, source and circumstances surrounding the videos cited by the APC. “However, it is important to state categorically that Governor Ademola Adeleke has neither authorised, participated in, directed nor endorsed the taking of any oath by anyone in relation to the August 15 governorship election or for any other political purpose,” he said. He described Adeleke as a democrat who believes in the freedom of citizens to make political choices based on their conscience. According to Salam, the governor’s campaign was based on his administration’s achievements, vision for Osun State and the confidence of the electorate, rather than intimidation or any alleged clandestine practices. “Governor Adeleke does not need oaths, threats, intimidation or any form of coercion to secure the support of the people of Osun State,” he added. The post Osun Election: APC, Adeleke campaign trade accusations over alleged oath-taking, vote buying appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La poésie d’El Hadji Malick Sy : l’amour du Prophète, le cœur de la spiritualité
items.description: Dans la plume d’El Hadji Malick Sy, l’amour du Prophète Muhammad n’est ni un simple élan de piété ni un thème poétique parmi d’autres. Il constitue, au contraire, le fondement même de son expérience spirituelle. À travers ses poèmes, le maître de Tivaouane montre que l’amour du Messager de Dieu est un chemin vers l’Absolu, une lumière qui éclaire le monde et une voie intérieure où se forme le croyant. El Hadji Malick Sy : Le poète méconnu Dans l’imaginaire collectif sénégalais, El Hadji Malick Sy est souvent présenté comme un grand érudit, un guide religieux ou encore un remarquable éducateur. On ignore souvent le talentueux poète qu’il fut et dont l’œuvre poétique révèle une autre facette, plus intime : celle d’un homme profondément habité par l’amour du Prophète Muhammad, point de passage absolu pour tout cheminement vers Dieu. Cet amour ne relève pas uniquement de l’émotion ou de la dévotion populaire. Il s’inscrit dans la tradition du soufisme, où la proximité avec Dieu passe par un attachement profond au Prophète. Dans cette perspective, aimer Muhammad n’est pas une fin en soi ; c’est la voie qui conduit à la Présence divine. Le Prophète : Une lumière au point zéro du commencement L’un des aspects les plus frappants de cette poésie est la façon dont El Hadji Malick Sy décrit le Prophète. Il ne se limite pas à la figure historique ayant vécu en Arabie au VIIᵉ siècle. Dans la tradition soufie qu’il épouse, Muhammad est également une réalité spirituelle primordiale. On se souvient tous de ses vers dans Khilâs al-Dhahab où El Hadji Malick Sy rappelle que Dieu avait déjà révélé au Prophète sa mission avant même la création d’Adam : « Dieu fit connaître à notre guide sa prophétie Alors qu’Adam était entre création du corps et souffle de l’âme. » Un autre vers du même poème nous apprend que toute la création trouve son origine dans le jaillissement de cette lumière prophétique :« En vérité, lorsqu’Allah eut le désir de nous créer, Il puisa dans Sa lumière la lumière du glorieux Prophète. » Le Prophète : source de toute miséricorde divine Pour El Hadji Malick Sy, à travers cette lumière, le Prophète est aussi le point de passage de la miséricorde de Dieu et irrigue la vie spirituelle des hommes. Cela s’explique par le fait que, pour le poète, rien n’aurait été créé sans le jaillissement de la lumière muhammadienne. Autrement dit, la miséricorde elle-même tire son origine de la lumière du Prophète. C’est ainsi que, dans la poésie d’El Hadji Malick Sy, le Prophète est décrit comme la source de la sagesse, des secrets spirituels et de la miséricorde divine. El Hadji Malick Sy écrit en ce sens :« Que Ta bénédiction soit sur le Prophète, l’essence de la miséricorde,la source des secrets spirituels, la lumière de la Sagesse universelle. » Dans cette vision de Maodo, Muhammad apparaît comme le lien privilégié entre Dieu et l’humanité. Il devient l’intermédiaire par lequel descendent la connaissance spirituelle, la miséricorde et les bienfaits divins. La prière sur le Prophète : une voie de transformation intérieure Dans la poésie d’El Hadji Malick Sy, invoquer le Prophète n’est jamais un simple exercice de répétition. La prière sur le Messager devient un véritable moyen de purification de l’âme, une voie d’intercession prophétique dans la quête de Dieu. Le voilà implorer Dieu en priant sur le Prophète de manière à solliciter sa médiation pour la réalisation spirituelle : « Par cette prière, purifie-nous de tout péché.Et par elle, fais-nous parvenir aux plus hauts degrés. » Dans un autre vers, il demande encore :« Bénis le Prophète d’une bénédiction par laquelle .Tu nous purifieras de nos péchés et nous élèveras au plus haut degré. »Ces vers montrent que la prière sur le Prophète est envisagée par El Hadji Malick Sy comme une véritable pédagogie spirituelle. Elle purifie le cœur, élève l’âme et rapproche progressivement le croyant de Dieu. L’amour du Prophète : l’assurance du salut L’un des vers les plus émouvants de cette poésie est sans doute celui où El Hadji Malick Sy reconnaît humblement que ses œuvres seules ne suffisent pas à espérer rencontrer Dieu, à parvenir à Sa présence sanctifiée et à atteindre la réalisation spirituelle. Toujours dans Khilâs, le maître de Tivaouane écrit :« Je n’ai commis aucun acte qui me permettrait de Te rencontrer, Dieu, ô Toi mon désir,Si ce n’est d’aimer, de glorifier et de me soumettre à Ton Prophète. » Dans cette poésie d’El Hadji Malick Sy, en quelques vers, toute une spiritualité se dévoile. En effet, le salut n’est pas présenté comme le fruit d’une performance religieuse, mais comme le résultat d’un amour sincère, d’une fidélité et d’une profonde humilité devant le modèle prophétique. Et cette voie, dégagée par El Hadji Malick Sy, demeure actuelle. Voilà que plus d’un siècle après la disparition de Maodo, cette vision continue de marquer profondément la culture religieuse sénégalaise. Les séances de prière sur le Prophète, les vers panégyriques chantés dans les foyers religieux, ou encore les grands rassemblements de Tivaouane et partout au Sénégal pour chanter la Burda en l’honneur du Prophète, puisent largement dans cet héritage d’El Hadji Malick Sy. L’œuvre du maître de Tivaouane rappelle aussi que, dans le soufisme sénégalais, la poésie n’est jamais une simple recherche esthétique. Elle devient une méthode d’éducation spirituelle, une manière de former le cœur autant que l’intelligence. Ainsi, en faisant de l’amour du Prophète le centre de sa vie intérieure, El Hadji Malick Sy offre une conception de la foi où la connaissance, la beauté et la quête de Dieu avancent ensemble, portées par la force des mots et la profondeur de l’amour prophétique. Par Dr Seydi Diamil NIANE,chargé de recherche en islamologie Institut fondamental d’Afrique noire Université Cheikh Anta Diop Email : seydidiamil.niane@ucad.edu.sn

items.title: « L’orchestre est une nécessité culturelle et sociale »
items.description: Créé en 2018, Jigeen Ñi, premier orchestre exclusivement féminin du Sénégal, s’est imposé comme un projet artistique au service de la promotion des femmes instrumentistes et du rayonnement culturel du pays. Son fondateur, Samba Diaité, également directeur du Partenariat et de la Coopération du Grand Théâtre national Doudou Ndiaye Coumba Rose, revient sur la genèse de cette initiative, les obstacles et son ambition. Qu’est-ce qui vous a convaincu, en 2018, qu’il était nécessaire de créer un orchestre entièrement composé de femmes instrumentistes ? L’idée est née d’un constat très simple. Le Sénégal compte d’excellentes musiciennes, mais elles sont rarement visibles lorsqu’il s’agit d’occuper les postes d’instrumentistes au sein des grands orchestres. La plupart du temps, les femmes sont cantonnées au chant ou aux chœurs, alors qu’elles possèdent toutes les compétences pour jouer du piano, de la batterie, de la basse ou des percussions avec un niveau professionnel. J’ai voulu créer un projet qui rompe avec cette réalité et qui démontre que les femmes peuvent porter, à elles seules, un orchestre de haut niveau. En 2018, cette idée est devenue réalité avec la naissance de Jigeen Ñi. Pourquoi avoir fait le choix d’un ensemble exclusivement féminin plutôt que d’un orchestre mixte ? Parce qu’il fallait envoyer un signal fort. Il ne s’agissait pas de créer un groupe féminin pour suivre une tendance, mais de répondre à une nécessité culturelle et sociale. Nous voulions montrer que le talent n’a ni sexe ni limite. Le nom « Jigeen Ñi », qui signifie les femmes en wolof, traduit parfaitement cette ambition. Notre objectif est de mettre en lumière les compétences des femmes musiciennes et de leur permettre d’occuper pleinement la place qui leur revient sur les scènes nationales et internationales. Justement, comment avez-vous constitué le premier noyau de musiciennes et quels critères ont guidé leur sélection ? Nous avons lancé un véritable travail de recherche. Nous avons rencontré de nombreuses musiciennes issues de différents horizons : conservatoires, écoles de musique, orchestres, familles de griots ou encore groupes professionnels. Très rapidement, Khady Dieng, pianiste et cheffe d’orchestre, s’est imposée comme un pilier du projet. Autour d’elle, une équipe soudée s’est progressivement constituée, partageant les mêmes valeurs de rigueur, de solidarité et de dépassement de soi. Aujourd’hui encore, cette exigence demeure notre principal critère de sélection. Quelle identité musicale avez-vous souhaité donner à Jigeen Ñi ? Notre ambition est de proposer une musique profondément enracinée dans les traditions sénégalaises tout en restant ouverte aux influences du monde. Nous travaillons autour des rythmes nationaux, de la musique mandingue, de la Casamance, de l’Afro-fusion, de la world music, du jazz et d’autres esthétiques contemporaines. Chaque concert est conçu comme un dialogue entre notre patrimoine culturel et les musiques actuelles. Nous voulons démontrer que la musique sénégalaise possède une richesse capable de dialoguer avec toutes les cultures. Au-delà de la dimension artistique, quel message cet orchestre entend-il porter auprès de la société sénégalaise ? Notre projet dépasse largement le cadre artistique. Jigeen Ñi défend l’égalité des chances, la valorisation des femmes, le respect, la paix, la solidarité et le vivre-ensemble. À travers cet orchestre, nous voulons encourager les jeunes filles à croire en leurs capacités et à poursuivre leurs ambitions, quelles qu’elles soient. Si demain une enfant décide d’apprendre la batterie, la basse ou le piano parce qu’elle a vu Jigeen Ñi sur scène, alors nous aurons atteint une partie de notre objectif. Pour conforter cette idée, nous avons lancé une académie destinée à former uniquement des jeunes dans le domaine du maniement des instruments. Les débuts ont-ils été marqués par des réticences ou des obstacles liés au caractère inédit du projet ? Comme tout projet innovant, nous avons dû convaincre. Beaucoup pensaient qu’un orchestre composé uniquement de femmes ne pourrait pas durer. Il a fallu gagner la confiance des partenaires, des organisateurs et parfois même du public. Les contraintes financières, les répétitions, la formation permanente et les déplacements représentaient également de véritables défis. Mais la qualité du travail, la discipline et la persévérance des musiciennes ont progressivement fait tomber tous les préjugés. Aujourd’hui, ces difficultés n’appartiennent pas encore au passé. Mais nous allons continuer le combat dans le but de relever ce défi titanesque à plus d’un titre. Huit ans après sa création, quel bilan tirez-vous du parcours de Jigeen Ñi et quelles sont, selon vous, les principales avancées obtenues ? Je ressens avant tout une immense fierté. Lorsque nous avons lancé ce projet en 2018, peu de personnes imaginaient que Jigeen Ñi représenterait un jour le Sénégal dans plusieurs pays européens. Aujourd’hui, le groupe participe à des festivals internationaux, effectue des résidences artistiques et bénéficie d’une reconnaissance qui dépasse largement nos espérances. Mais ce succès est surtout celui des musiciennes, qui ont travaillé sans relâche pour imposer leur talent. Le plus beau reste sans doute les témoignages des jeunes filles qui nous disent qu’elles veulent devenir musiciennes après avoir assisté à nos concerts. Aujourd’hui, l’orchestre joue presque partout dans le monde. Quelles sont désormais les priorités de développement de Jigeen Ñi et les grandes ambitions que vous nourrissez pour les prochaines années ? Nous voulons poursuivre l’internationalisation du groupe en participant à davantage de festivals et de tournées sur les différents continents. Nous préparons également de nouvelles créations musicales, des collaborations avec des artistes étrangers ainsi que plusieurs projets pédagogiques destinés à accompagner la formation de jeunes musiciennes sénégalaises. Notre ambition est aussi de faire de Jigeen Ñi une véritable institution culturelle capable de transmettre son expérience aux générations futures. Nous souhaitons enfin contribuer au rayonnement du Sénégal à travers une diplomatie culturelle fondée sur l’excellence artistique.Je remercie toutes les personnes qui ont cru en cette aventure depuis le premier jour. Jigeen Ñi est la preuve que lorsqu’on fait confiance aux femmes, qu’on leur donne les moyens de s’exprimer et qu’on place l’exigence artistique au cœur d’un projet, les résultats peuvent dépasser toutes les attentes. Notre plus grande ambition est de continuer à porter haut les couleurs du Sénégal et de montrer, partout dans le monde, que notre pays possède des artistes d’un immense talent et une culture capable de rassembler les peuples autour des mêmes valeurs de paix, de dialogue et de fraternité. Entretien réalisé par Adama NDIAYE

items.title: Nefza | Vaste campagne pour libérer les plages du domaine public maritime
items.description: Dans le cadre de la sécurisation de la saison touristique et de la protection du domaine public maritime, une vaste campagne conjointe s'est déroulée ce jeudi 6 août 2026 sur les plages de Zouaraa, El Magassib et Cap Negro, situées dans la délégation de Nefza. Placée sous la supervision du gouvernorat de Béja, cette opération vise à éradiquer toutes les formes d'installation anarchique et à garantir un accès libre et agréable à tous les estivants. L'initiative a mobilisé un large éventail d'acteurs régionaux et sécuritaires notamment les unités e la garde nationale de Tabarka et de Bizerte, l'antenne régionale de Béja de l'Agence de Protection et d'Aménagement du Littoral (Apal), la Direction régionale du Commerce de Béja, ou encore les services régionaux de l'Instance nationale de la sécurité sanitaire des produit salimentaires (INSSPA). L'intervention s'est soldée par la verbalisation de plusieurs infractions et la rédaction de procès-verbaux judiciaires, précise l'Apal dans son communiqué en affirmant que cette campagne s'inscrit dans une démarche globale visant à faire respecter la réglementation régissant l'exploitation du domaine public maritime, à preserver l'esthétique et l'environnement des plages de la région et à garantir le droit des citoyens à profiter du littoral dans des conditions optimales de confort et de sécurité. Ex-Oyo City Boy coordinator quits movement, vows support for Tinubu, 2027 bid
items.description: By Adeola Badru The former Oyo State Coordinator of the City Boy Movement, Ahmed Ajibola, popularly known as General H, has resigned from the group, citing differences over the direction of its state structure. Ajibola, however, said his resignation had not affected his support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda, including the President’s bid for re-election in 2027. He disclosed his resignation in a statement posted on Instagram on Friday, while also denying reports circulating on social media that he had been removed as the movement’s Oyo State coordinator or made derogatory remarks about President Tinubu, Seyi Tinubu and other leaders of the organisation. Ajibola described the reports as “false, malicious and misleading”, insisting that he was neither dismissed, suspended nor removed from office, but voluntarily resigned after declining two separate appointments offered to him by the movement. According to him, he was first appointed Coordinator, Directorate Affairs, at the state level by the Oyo State Director on August 1, 2026, before receiving another appointment from the national leadership on August 5 as Coordinator, Stakeholder Engagement, South-West Structure. He said he rejected both appointments before subsequently tendering his resignation from the movement. “If I had truly been sacked, where is the letter of dismissal, termination, or removal from office? None exists because none was ever issued,” he said. In his resignation letter addressed to the national leadership of the movement, Ajibola expressed gratitude for the opportunity to serve in Oyo State but said he had decided not to accept the new positions offered to him. He maintained that his decision was based on principle rather than resentment. “My decision is based not on bitterness, but on principle,” he said. Ajibola said he believed leadership should be founded on “fairness, loyalty, transparency, competence and mutual respect”, adding that developments within the Oyo State structure had made it difficult for him to continue with the movement “in good conscience”. He said he had become increasingly dissatisfied with the direction of the movement at the state level, particularly under its newly appointed leadership. “Certain actions and decisions have fallen short of the values that inspired many of us to dedicate our time, energy and resources to the growth of this movement,” he said. However, Ajibola drew a distinction between his departure from the City Boy Movement and his political support for President Tinubu, insisting that his resignation should not be interpreted as a rejection of the President or his administration. “Let me, however, make one thing abundantly clear: my resignation from the City Boy Movement does not in any way diminish my support, admiration and loyalty to His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR,” he said. He said he remained committed to promoting the achievements of the Tinubu administration and the Renewed Hope Agenda, while pledging to continue supporting the President’s re-election bid in 2027. “My conviction remains unchanged, and my support remains unwavering,” he added. The former Oyo coordinator also denied allegations that he had attacked or made derogatory comments about President Tinubu, Seyi Tinubu, the Director-General or other members of the movement’s national leadership. He challenged those behind the allegations to produce evidence to substantiate their claims, describing the accusations as part of what he called a false narrative surrounding his resignation. Ajibola urged members of the public to disregard the allegations, insisting that he did not leave the organisation out of hostility towards its national leadership. Reflecting on his time with the movement, he expressed appreciation to members who worked with him across Oyo State and acknowledged their loyalty, commitment and sacrifices. “I believe that positions may be given and positions may be taken away, but character, integrity and service remain permanent. “Therefore, I have chosen to step away with my dignity intact, my conscience clear and my gratitude unwavering towards those who believed in me and stood beside me throughout this journey,” he said. Ajibola said he remained proud of the achievements recorded with members of the movement during his tenure and thanked them for their support and sacrifices. items.title: EFCC can freeze state accounts, must obtain court order within 72 hours — Falana
items.description: ABUJA — Human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Femi Falana, has said the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) acted within its statutory powers by placing restrictions on the Osun State Government’s account. Falana, who spoke on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, said the commission could place a Post No Debit (PND) restriction on a state government account, provided it obtained a court order within the period prescribed by law. According to him, the legal authority of the EFCC to impose such restrictions had already been affirmed by the courts. He cited a 2022 judgment of the Court of Appeal in a case involving the Benue State Government and the EFCC, saying the decision established that the commission could impose a PND restriction for up to 72 hours pending an application to court. “Well, as far as the law is concerned, the EFCC has not acted illegally. As a matter of fact, that came out in the statement of the President: ‘I’m not questioning your mandate and the exercise of your power. However, I’m embarrassed,’” Falana said. He maintained that the EFCC had the authority to restrict access to the accounts of the Federal Government, state governments and local governments, subject to compliance with the relevant legal requirements. “Under the law, the EFCC has the power to freeze the account of the Federal Government or of any state or local government in Nigeria,” he said. Falana cites Benue case Falana recalled that the Federal High Court in Benue State had, in 2019, ruled against the EFCC in a case concerning the freezing of the state government’s account and awarded N50 million in damages against the commission. He said the EFCC appealed the decision, leading to a judgment by the Court of Appeal in September 2022. According to Falana, the appellate court overturned the earlier position and affirmed the commission’s power to impose a PND restriction on a government account, provided it approached the court within 72 hours. “That remains the law in Nigeria today,” he said. Supreme Court ruling The SAN also referred to a 2024 Supreme Court judgment arising from a suit filed by the Kogi State Government and other states challenging the authority of anti-corruption agencies to investigate state government accounts. Falana said the apex court examined the relevant constitutional and statutory provisions and affirmed the powers of agencies including the EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and Nigeria Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU) to investigate accounts. “In 2024, the Kogi State Government, joined by many state governments, challenged the investigation—probing of state accounts by EFCC, ICPC or NFIU. And in a historic judgment, the Supreme Court examined all the relevant laws and came to the conclusion that these agencies have the power to probe the accounts of any organisation, either at the federal, state or local government level. That remains the law in Nigeria,” he said. Falana said any move to alter the existing legal framework should be pursued through the National Assembly. “If Nigerians—those who are concerned—want the law changed, they can go to the National Assembly. But for now, as of today, EFCC has the power to freeze the account of any state and, in not more than 72 hours, has to go to court,” he said. items.title: Chidoka seeks new national consensus on equal citizenship, accountable power
items.description: By Our Correspondent PORT HARCOURT — A former Minister of Aviation and Chancellor of the Athena Centre for Policy and Leadership, Osita Chidoka, has called for a new national consensus founded on equal citizenship, accountable public power and a shared responsibility to defend the rights of every Nigerian. Chidoka made the call while delivering the keynote address at the 28th Wole Soyinka Lecture in Port Harcourt, which also featured the inauguration of the National Association of Seadogs’ Martyrs’ Day. Professor Wole Soyinka, who turned 92, was present throughout the lecture. The lecture series was established in 1994 by the National Association of Seadogs (NAS), also known as Pyrates Confraternity, to mark Soyinka’s 60th birthday. It has since become an annual platform for discussions on good governance, social justice and democratic ideals. NAS was founded in 1952 at the University College, Ibadan, by seven undergraduates, including Soyinka, and was formally registered in 1980. The inaugural Martyrs’ Day honours 33 NAS members who were detained for 72 days in Port Harcourt in 1997, an episode Chidoka examined extensively in his address. Speaking on the theme, “Reclaiming the Nigerian State Through Accountability, Justice and Civic Courage,” Chidoka argued that Nigeria’s challenges go beyond the structure of the federation. He said the country lacked “a sufficiently shared organising ideal” and needed a common understanding of “what Nigerian power is for, what citizenship must guarantee and what Nigerians owe one another.” Chidoka acknowledged the need to reform Nigeria’s federal arrangements, particularly in the areas of devolution, policing and fiscal responsibility, but cautioned that structural reforms without a corresponding moral purpose could merely redistribute injustice. “A federation can be decentralised and still be unjust. A regional government can oppress a local minority. A state police service can protect a Governor rather than the citizen,” he said. Tracing Nigeria’s founding aspirations through the 1957 Willink Commission, the independence anthem and the 1999 Constitution, Chidoka said the country was established on a promise to protect minorities, uphold justice and build a nation in which no citizen would be oppressed. He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for restoring “Nigeria, We Hail Thee” as the national anthem in 2024, arguing that the anthem “does more than ask us to love Nigeria: it tells us what kind of Nigeria deserves our loyalty.” Chidoka proposed three commitments as the foundation of a renewed national consensus: equal citizenship without the need for an ethnic sponsor or political godfather; public power treated as a trust that leaves a trail and submits to correction; and a shared duty to defend the dignity of Nigerians regardless of their party, faith or community. Accountability must have consequences — Chidoka On accountability, which he defined as “answerability joined to consequence,” Chidoka, drawing from his experience as Corps Marshal of the Federal Road Safety Corps, said explanations, audit reports and court judgments were insufficient without corrective action. “Explanation without correction is not accountability,” he said, proposing a three-part discipline for public power: “trace, test, correct.” Drawing a link between the 1997 detention of NAS members in Port Harcourt and the 2005 killing of the Apo Six in Abuja, Chidoka argued that Nigeria had changed the “uniform of its rulers” without sufficiently changing the reflexes of power. He urged NAS to broaden the meaning of Martyrs’ Day beyond its members, insisting that “the best way to honour the F18 survivors is to defend citizens who do not belong to this Association.” Chidoka called for a national consensus that would promote equal citizenship, accountable public power and a shared sense of responsibility. “Let us construct a new national consensus around equal citizenship, answerable power and common brotherhood. Let us give young Nigerians a banner worth carrying. Let us build a Nigeria where courage can live and no citizen needs a martyr’s bravery merely to enjoy a citizen’s rights,” he said. items.title: CHU de Bogodogo : Un an après leur naissance, les quintuplés Zerbo célèbrent leur premier anniversaire
items.description: Le service social du Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) de Bogodogo a célébré, ce 7 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, le premier anniversaire des quintuplés de la famille Zerbo. Nés prématurément dans la nuit du 16 au 17 juin 2025, ces cinq enfants, dont la survie relevait d'un défi médical majeur, se portent aujourd'hui bien grâce à une prise en charge multidisciplinaire. Le Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) de Bogodogo a vécu un moment riche en émotion en célébrant le premier anniversaire des quintuplés de la famille Zerbo. Cette cérémonie a réuni les équipes de gynécologie-obstétrique, de pédiatrie, de néonatologie, le service social ainsi que les parents des enfants, venus rendre grâce pour ce parcours exceptionnel. Pour les soignants, cette célébration symbolise l'aboutissement d'une année de suivi intensif et la réussite d'une prise en charge qui, au départ, était loin d'être gagnée. Selon Dr Madeleine Dabiré, gynécologue-obstétricienne au CHU de Bogodogo, la mère des quintuplés a été admise dans la nuit du 16 au 17 juin 2025 avec « une grossesse multiple à risque ». Après une prise en charge rapide par les équipes médicales, les cinq bébés sont nés par césarienne à seulement sept mois de grossesse. La spécialiste explique que les grossesses multiples exposent aussi bien la mère que les enfants à d'importantes complications. Dans le cas des quintuplés, un seul placenta devait assurer les besoins nutritionnels des cinq fœtus, une situation susceptible de compromettre leur développement et même d'entraîner une interruption de la grossesse. À cela s'est ajoutée une complication liée à l'hypertension artérielle, l'éclampsie, qui a provoqué un accouchement prématuré. « La prématurité, c'est quand même un risque de fragilité pour ces enfants. Donc, ce n'était pas évident qu'on puisse les voir vivants à cet âge-là. Les voir aujourd'hui célébrer leur premier anniversaire est vraiment une immense joie pour nous » , a confié le Dr Madeleine Dabiré. Un an après leur naissance, les cinq enfants sont en bonne santé. Une évolution que les responsables du CHU attribuent à l'engagement des équipes de gynécologie-obstétrique, de néonatologie, de pédiatrie ainsi qu'au suivi assuré par le service social. Pour le Dr Solange Odile Ouédraogo/Yougbaré, chef du service de pédiatrie, cette naissance restera gravée dans l'histoire de l'établissement. « Dans le service, nous accueillons régulièrement des jumeaux et des triplés. Mais depuis l'ouverture du CHU en 2017, nous n'avions encore jamais enregistré de quintuplés. C'était une première, et tout s'est bien passé. Nous avons donc tenu à célébrer ce premier anniversaire avec toute l'équipe et la famille », a-t-elle déclaré. Les quintuplés de la famille Zerbo©️Faso7 Au-delà des soins médicaux, le service social du CHU a mis en place un accompagnement spécifique afin d'assurer le suivi des enfants et d'apporter un soutien à leurs parents. Selon Perpétue Toé, chef du service social, dès l'arrivée de la famille, l'ensemble des équipes, sous la coordination du directeur général du CHU, s'est mobilisé pour offrir une prise en charge globale. « Nous voulions nous assurer que la famille bénéficiait d'un accompagnement adéquat et qu'elle pouvait assurer le suivi médical des enfants dans les meilleures conditions », a-t-elle expliqué. Très ému, Boureima Zerbo, père des quintuplés, a exprimé sa profonde reconnaissance envers le personnel du CHU de Bogodogo. « Depuis que nous sommes arrivés à Bogodogo, nous n'avons jamais eu besoin d'aller ailleurs pour un examen. Tous les soins ont été réalisés ici et entièrement pris en charge. Les enfants sont restés au service de néonatologie jusqu'à aujourd'hui. Au nom de toute notre famille, nous remercions la direction générale du CHU et l'ensemble des équipes de soins » , a-t-il déclaré. Cette célébration marque non seulement le premier anniversaire des quintuplés de la famille Zerbo, mais aussi une réussite médicale et humaine pour le CHU de Bogodogo, illustrant l'engagement des professionnels de santé burkinabè dans la prise en charge des grossesses à haut risque et des nouveau-nés prématurés. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article CHU de Bogodogo : Un an après leur naissance, les quintuplés Zerbo célèbrent leur premier anniversaire est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Trump’s Déjà-Vu Moment on Birthright Citizenship
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. If at first you don’t succeed, appeal to a higher federal court. And if you even lose at the Supreme Court … just try again anyway. This seems to be President Trump’s approach to limiting birthright citizenship. Last year, he issued an executive order that purports to end the practice of automatically granting citizenship to babies born in the United States—as has been the norm since the late 19th century. Despite Trump visiting oral arguments in an apparent attempt to intimidate the justices, the Supreme Court struck down the order this June. Yesterday, Trump attempted to do some of the same things via new executive orders. One is intended to deny automatic citizenship to children born to people living in the United States while working for a foreign government and children of people declared to be terrorists or adversaries of the U.S. It would also deny citizenship to people born in U.S. territories if Congress passes a proposed law allowing that, creating a new group of stateless people. The second order is intended to prevent the practice of “birth tourism,” in which people visiting the United States on tourist visas give birth to babies who are then U.S. citizens. Legal experts and advocates say the orders are unconstitutional, and they are certain to be challenged in court. Trump’s loss at the Supreme Court seems to make these orders a long shot. As Chief Justice John Roberts wrote in his opinion for the Court , “children born of parents unlawfully or temporarily present in the United States” satisfy the relevant conditions and thus “under the Constitution, they are citizens at birth.” The language in the orders about “alien enemies” is another likely area for dispute, not because anyone is eager to welcome the children of bona fide adversaries but because this administration has made absurd claims about illegal immigration constituting an “invasion,” which makes no sense on its face and has been rejected by federal judges. Trump’s announcement of the orders at the White House yesterday was full of fabrications, exaggerations, and lies. Trump claimed that the Fourteenth Amendment “was meant for the babies of slaves. It was—it was right after—one week or two weeks after the Civil War ended.” In fact, it passed three years later, in 1868. The presidential adviser Stephen Miller echoed the same idea, saying that the amendment “had no other meaning and purpose outside of that, and that’s been clear, obviously, since the day that it was passed.” When a politician uses the word obviously —like frankly —that’s a good sign that what follows will be neither obvious nor true. If this had been obvious since 1868, the U.S. wouldn’t have acted otherwise for more than a century, and the Supreme Court would have ruled in favor of the administration. Trump’s claims about birth tourism were even further off base. The president isn’t making the idea up—just wildly exaggerating it. Asked by a reporter how many people are engaging in the practice, Trump said, “I can tell you right now. Hundreds of thousands. Hundreds of thousands.” This number appears to be pulled out of thin air. During Supreme Court oral arguments, Solicitor General John Sauer, arguing on behalf of Trump, was asked how commonly birth tourism occurs and replied, “No one knows for sure.” In 2020, the Center for Immigration Studies, which supports much stricter laws, estimated the number at between 20,000 and 26,000 births each year, out of roughly 3.6 million babies born in the United States. By attempting to end or restrict birthright citizenship in order to address these issues, Trump is trying to use a bulldozer to achieve a task that calls for a small mallet. The law already prohibits fraudulent visa applications, and the Justice Department has prosecuted people for birth tourism in the past. Trying to undermine birthright citizenship risks jettisoning one of the fundamental bases of modern American society to deal with a minor challenge. Trump could have tried another path. Justice Brett Kavanaugh offered the White House a potential lifeline in his concurrence in the birthright case, suggesting that despite the plain language of the Fourteenth Amendment, Congress could pass a law altering birthright citizenship. The likelihood of such a bill succeeding seems very low, and pushing it through would require sustained attention from Trump. Instead, he’s trying to achieve his goals through executive orders, which are both easily reversed by a future president and have already proved unsuccessful. But the president has a demonstrated weakness for this kind of grand, overreaching presidential gesture. Last month, after a member of the U.S. men’s national soccer team was suspended for a game in the World Cup, Trump decided to use his position to exert some pressure , calling FIFA President Gianni Infantino to try to get the suspension waived. In a direct sense, it worked—FIFA allowed the player to participate—but it may have backfired. Belgium, the American opponent, was incensed, and trounced the United States 4–1. Trump ended up looking obnoxious and corrupt, but didn’t even get a victory out of it. The player in question, by the way, was Folarin Balogun—a U.S. citizen by birth because his mother, while pregnant and visiting family, got stuck in the United States. Evening Read Illustration by Dena Springer A Chatbot-Free Childhood Will Be a Status Symbol By Dana Suskind The human brain has evolved to learn from specific instructors. When a child hears a gentle spoken word or a soothing lullaby from another person, when their cry is responded to, their brain lights up. Nurturing interactions, or what child-development experts call “serve and return” exchanges, help shape and strengthen the 1 million new neural connections taking place in a child’s brain every single second. Every time a child cries or serves up a bid for attention and receives a caregiver’s response, that back-and-forth helps build the circuits underlying their communication, learning, and emotional well-being. No other input, not even Johann Pachelbel’s Canon in D performed by the Berlin Philharmonic, is capable of activating the neural circuitry the way human interaction does. Until now. items.title: Fada N’Gourma : Le CICR mise sur les médias pour renforcer l’accès à une information humanitaire de qualité
items.description: Le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) a réuni, le mercredi 5 août 2026 à Fada N’Gourma, des journalistes des régions du Grand Est et du Nakambé pour un atelier d’échanges consacré à l’action humanitaire. Cette rencontre, couplée à une visite de terrain, visait à permettre aux professionnels des médias de mieux comprendre les interventions du Mouvement international de la Croix-Rouge et du Croissant-Rouge au Burkina Faso, afin de diffuser une information plus juste et plus utile aux populations. Au cours de cette immersion, les journalistes ont découvert plusieurs réalisations du CICR dans la région de l’Est. Première étape, le Centre hospitalier régional universitaire (CHRU) de Fada N’Gourma, où l’organisation intervient depuis 2022 pour renforcer la prise en charge des blessés. L’appui porte notamment sur la fourniture de consommables médicaux, le renforcement des capacités du personnel soignant ainsi que la construction d’un Centre de récupération et d’éducation nutritionnelle (CREN). Pour Jean-Louis Bamboulé, Professeur chirurgien et représentant du directeur général du CHRU, ce partenariat a considérablement renforcé les capacités de l’établissement. « Le CICR est un partenaire déterminé venu en appui au CHRU de Fada », Jean-Louis Bamboulé « Le CICR est un partenaire déterminé venu en appui au CHRU de Fada, qui accueille un nombre important de patients. En plus des médicaments, il y a des infrastructures et des sessions de renforcement des capacités au profit des agents », a-t-il souligné. La délégation s’est ensuite rendue au Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) du secteur 11, désormais érigé en Centre médical urbain grâce à l’accompagnement du CICR. Dans cette zone qui accueille un grand nombre de personnes déplacées internes, l’organisation a également réalisé un forage d’un débit de 2,10 m³ par heure afin d'améliorer l’accès à l’eau potable. Cette infrastructure, inscrite dans les actions Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (WASH), contribue à répondre aux besoins essentiels des communautés vulnérables. Les bénéficiaires rencontrés sur place ont exprimé leur satisfaction et leur gratitude envers le CICR, saluant des interventions qui améliorent concrètement leurs conditions de vie. Pour Zalissa Sanfo, chargée de communication publique au CICR, cette initiative répond à une volonté de rapprocher les journalistes des réalités du terrain afin qu’ils puissent mieux relayer les enjeux humanitaires. « Avec les journalistes, nous avons fait le plaidoyer pour que la bonne information puisse accéder aux personnes », Zalissa Sanfo « Avec les journalistes, nous avons fait le plaidoyer pour que la bonne information puisse accéder aux personnes. La bonne information, au bon moment, à la bonne personne, peut être perçue comme une aide humanitaire et peut sauver une vie » , a-t-elle déclaré. Au-delà de la visite des réalisations, les participants ont bénéficié d'une présentation sur les principes, les missions et le fonctionnement du Mouvement international de la Croix-Rouge et du Croissant-Rouge. Ils ont également été informés de l’organisation prochaine du concours de reportage humanitaire du CICR, une initiative destinée à encourager les productions médiatiques mettant en lumière les questions humanitaires et les défis auxquels font face les populations affectées. À travers cette rencontre, le CICR réaffirme sa conviction que les médias constituent des partenaires essentiels dans la diffusion d'une information fiable, responsable et susceptible de contribuer à la protection des populations en situation de vulnérabilité. items.title: Luv FM High School Debate: Twenty schools get set to battle for 2026 crown
items.description: Twenty Senior High Schools in the Ashanti Region are set to compete for the ultimate prize in the eighth edition of the LUV FM High School Debate, powered by Kelcharcoal. The annual intellectual competition begins on Monday, August 10, 2026, after more than 100 schools participated in preliminary contests held across the region. The schools were grouped into zones during the preliminary phase, with the top 20 emerging as finalists after a series of competitive debates. The finalists will compete by demonstrating their skills in public speaking, critical thinking and teamwork, with judges assessing participants based on the structure and clarity of arguments, presentation skills, technical accuracy and overall delivery. Relationship Manager at LUV FM, Maxwell Frimpong-Manso, said the competition has grown into an important platform for developing young people beyond the classroom. “Over the years, the LUV FM Kelcharcoal debate has grown in stature and impact. While only one school will be crowned, every participant will leave with valuable knowledge and confidence. Multimedia remains committed to providing quality content and empowering our communities.” Chairperson and Ambassador of the LUV FM High School Debate, Theodosia Jackson, said the increasing participation from schools reflects the relevance and popularity of the programme. She encouraged more schools to join future editions, describing the debate as a platform that helps students build confidence and prepare for future challenges. “The competition, I have realised, has attracted many participants. It shows the programme’s popularity and interest. We are asking schools to register and take advantage of gaining knowledge, confidence and boldness to face challenges in life. It is a training ground for our students.” Lead Judge and Senior Lecturer at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) Department of English, Dr Peter Arthur, said the judging process this year would focus more on the technical strength of arguments. He explained that participants would be assessed beyond emotional appeal, with emphasis placed on logic, organisation and evidence-based presentations. “This year, we will look out for technicalities and focus also on the structure of arguments rather than emotions. The expectation is very high. They are smart, and so it leaves us with a lot to expect.” Regional SRC President, Hope Arthur James, said the partnership between the Ashanti Regional Students’ Council and LUV FM has helped create opportunities for students to develop their communication skills. “Our commitment as ARSRC was to advocate for students and liaise between institutions and the student body. LUV FM-Kelcharcoal provided a very viable space for us to materialise that commitment. The past eight years have been able to bring out the best in Ashanti Regional students.” The 2026 edition is sponsored by Kelcharcoal toothpaste, Didi Shito, Bigoo, The Seed Travelz, Serpo Mystical Pen, Verna Mineral Water, Jackson University College, Tamak, St. Ben Jewelry, Otuasekan Community Bank and New Generation Investment Services. Organisers say the debate remains committed to nurturing young talents and providing students with a platform to sharpen skills that are essential for leadership and national development.

items.title: Gender Minister begins Northern Region tour to monitor LEAP enrolment exercise
items.description: The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has begun a three-day working visit to the Northern and North East regions to monitor the ongoing Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty (LEAP) beneficiary enrolment exercise and engage key stakeholders on the implementation of the programme. The Minister is accompanied by members of the Ministry’s Advisory Board and senior management staff as part of the exercise, which is aimed at assessing the progress of the nationwide LEAP enrolment and expansion programme. As part of the first day’s activities, Dr Lartey paid a courtesy call on the Chief of Fuo, Abdulai Neindow, in the Sagnarigu Municipality before visiting the community’s LEAP enrolment centre. At the enrolment centre, she interacted with beneficiaries, registration officials and community members while observing the registration process to assess the efficiency of operations and ensure that eligible households are enrolled in a transparent and orderly manner. Addressing the media, the Minister said the monitoring exercise forms part of the Ministry’s commitment to ensuring the successful implementation of the expanded LEAP programme, which seeks to enrol an additional 400,000 beneficiary households across the country. She explained that the exercise provides an opportunity to assess field operations, identify operational challenges and implement timely interventions to improve service delivery. Dr Lartey also highlighted the importance of the nationwide LEAP reassessment, noting that it is intended to update beneficiary data, strengthen the integrity of the programme and ensure that support reaches the most vulnerable households. According to her, the reassessment will help minimise inclusion and exclusion errors while promoting fairness, accountability and effective targeting of social protection interventions. The Minister’s three-day tour will also include engagements with stakeholders across the Northern and North East regions, as well as a visit to the Gambaga Alleged Witches Camp.

items.title: Crise migratoire à Sebta : l’AMDH réclame une enquête pour déterminer les responsabilités
items.description: L'Association marocaine des droits humains (AMDH) a appelé, vendredi, à l’ouverture d’une enquête indépendante et globale concernant les événements de Sebta et Melilla occupées survenus les 30 et 31 juillet. Selon l'association, le bilan des morts s'élèverait à 141 cas et 11 nationalités arabes faisaient partie des migrants. Lors d'une conférence de presse organisée au siège de l’AMDH à Rabat, en partenariat avec la Coordination européenne pour les droits humains au Maroc, l'organisation a appelé à déterminer les différentes responsabilités, élucider les circonstances des événements précités et décider des suites juridiques. La présidente de l’AMDH, Souad Brahma, a en ce sens estimé que sur la base des témoignages recueillis auprès des personnes revenues et du suivi effectué par les acteurs de terrain, « le nombre annoncé de victimes ne reflète pas la réalité ». Selon les chiffres avancés par l'association, le bilan des décès suivant les tentatives de rejoindre Sebta occupée serait de 141 morts. Pour l'AMDH, ces événements « ne constituent pas seulement une tentative de franchissement de frontière, mais révèlent la profondeur de la crise sociale au Maroc », avec une dimension politique marquée par « l’effondrement des institutions de médiation et l’affaiblissement du rôle d’encadrement des partis politiques et des syndicats » . Souad Brahma a affirmé que « les événements tragiques de Sebta et Melilla occupées nécessitent l’ouverture d’une enquête indépendante et transparente », considérant qu’ils traduisent « une crise et un échec des politiques publiques, au point que la mer est devenue plus clémente que l’État ». Qualifiant les faits de « grande tragédie humaine », l'organisation de défense des droits humains a critiqué l’absence de proclamation d’un deuil national. Par ailleurs, la présidente a pointé du doigt l’explication avancée par le porte-parole du ministère de l’Intérieur, qui avait évoqué l’implication de réseaux de traite des êtres humains. Elle a considéré que cela s'apparentait à un recours à « la théorie du complot », tout en critiquant que les personnes revenues soient confrontées à l’emprisonnement plutôt qu’à une prise en charge. En ce sens, l'AMDH et la Coordination européenne pour les droits humains au Maroc ont également fait état de la situation judiciaire de plusieurs candidats à la migration. Selon elles, 59 personnes sont placées en détention provisoire à Tétouan, dont 5 mineurs, tandis que 52 autres sont détenues à Nador, parmi lesquelles 18 mineurs placés dans un centre de protection de l’enfance. Elles évoquent également 11 personnes poursuivies devant la Cour d’appel de Nador pour des chefs d’accusation criminels, notamment entrave à la circulation, violences contre des agents publics et rébellion collective. De son côté, Achraf Maimoun, président de la section de l’AMDH à Tétouan, a affirmé que « la tragédie avait commencé avant le 30 juillet », en soulignant qu’une tentative de franchissement impliquant plus de 500 personnes avait été enregistrée le 27 juillet, selon des données documentées par la partie espagnole de Sebta occupée. A ce titre, il a signalé que des familles contactaient l’association depuis mai dernier pour signaler qu’elles n’avaient toujours pas récupéré les corps de leurs proches. Le représentant associatif a également estimé que la partie marocaine « n’avait pas lancé une opération de recherche massive des corps » , en se limitant selon lui à récupérer les dépouilles flottant à la surface de l’eau. Il a déclaré qu'actuellement 21 corps se trouvaient dans une morgue, dont ceux de migrants issus de 11 nationalités arabes. « Ce ne sont pas des chiffres, ce sont des personnes qui avaient des rêves et qui voulaient vivre dignement », a-t-il déclaré, estimant qu’elles avaient péri « devant les autorités des deux pays, sans intervention qui aurait pu réduire le nombre de victimes » . Dans les documents distribués lors de la conférence de presse, l’AMDH a également avancé le rôle et l'impact des politiques européennes en matière de migration dans ces événements. L'AMDH a ainsi critiqué « les politiques européennes jugées inhumaines dans la gestion des questions migratoires » , estimant qu’elles auraient transformé les migrants en « instrument politique utilisé par certaines forces de droite européennes pour renforcer leur influence et masquer les véritables causes des crises sociales touchant une partie des populations européennes » . Enfin, l'association a estimé que « la tragédie de Sebta et Melilla ne peut être dissociée de la nature inégale et injuste des relations entre les pays du Nord et du Sud, et des déséquilibres économiques et sociaux qui en résultent » . items.title: 2027: Kefas picks APC women leader as running mate
items.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — Taraba State Governor, Dr Agbu Kefas, has indicated that the Deputy National Women Leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Zainab Ibrahim, may be his running mate in the 2027 governorship election. Kefas made the disclosure on Friday at the TY Danjuma House in Jalingo while hosting the National Chairman of the APC, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda. Yilwatda was in the state to celebrate his 58th birthday. While recognising dignitaries during the protocol session, Governor Kefas referred to Ibrahim as the “future deputy governor of Taraba State”, a description also used by the APC national chairman, who addressed her as the “incoming deputy governor”. In his remarks, Kefas expressed appreciation to the APC leadership for organising a state-wide medical outreach as part of activities marking Yilwatda’s birthday. According to him, “Your team of doctors for the free treatment and surgeries has been on the ground working for days, and the testimonies from the people of Taraba State are deeply impressive. “For us in Taraba State, we are all for the APC to pay back what Mr President has done for us. “What President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has done for the people of Taraba cannot be quantified. “Mr President recently approved an Army division for us, which alone is capable of stabilising the state. Mr Chairman, here in Taraba, we in the APC are not contesting elections with anybody. We only have people participating with us.” Speaking earlier, Yilwatda explained that he chose Taraba State for his 58th birthday celebration to demonstrate the party’s commitment to the welfare of citizens. According to him, “APC does not only canvass for votes but also show the human face of our party. “We do not only knock on doors for votes, but we care for the people’s health, education and future.” He also commended Governor Kefas for aligning with the ruling party, noting that President Tinubu prioritises inclusive development irrespective of past electoral outcomes. The post 2027: Kefas picks APC women leader as running mate appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nouveau BMS canicule en Algérie : jusqu’à 45°C, les régions concernées
items.description: Les alertes à la canicule se succèdent en Algérie. Depuis un mois, la vague de chaleur frappe de plein fouet plusieurs régions du pays. Le dernier BMS (bulletin météorologique spécial) de canicule en date a été lancé ce vendredi 7 août par l’Office national de la météo (ONM). Placée sous vigilance orange canicule (niveau II), Bejaïa, Skikda, Annaba, El Tarf et Jijel. Ces cinq wilayas du littoral seront confrontées à des températures élevées de 40°C à 42°C dans la journée, et de 26°C à 28°C dans la soirée, et ce du dimanche au lundi 10 août. Algérie : canicule et incendies, un été pourri La deuxième alerte lancée par l’ONM concerne les wilayas de Chlef, Relizane et Aïn Defla, où les températures peuvent atteindre 45°C dans la journée. En soirée, il fera très chaud et le mercure pourrait grimper jusqu’à 30°C, et ce durant trois jours : samedi, dimanche 09 et lundi 10 août. Cette nouvelle vague de chaleur qui touche huit wilayas du pays survient alors que les incendies continuent de ravager les forêts du pays. Ce vendredi, dans son dernier point de situation, la Protection civile a indiqué avoir enregistré 15 incendies, dont 12 ont été éteints et trois sont toujours en activité à Tipaza, Jijel et Souk Ahras. items.title: Patchbay Band to share their story on E Vibes this August
items.description: Patchbay Band, one of Ghana’s most celebrated live music ensembles, will feature on E Vibes this August, sharing the story behind their remarkable journey and contributions to Ghana’s music industry. Like a patchbay in a recording studio that connects different instruments, hardware and signals into one unified sound, Patchbay Band has become a musical connector in its own right. Formed in 2008 by bassist and music director Philip Acquah, the Accra-based band is renowned for blending traditional Ghanaian highlife with jazz, blues and indie rock. The award-winning group has headlined performances at the iconic +233 Jazz Bar, served as the backing band for the Ghana Music Awards, and shared the stage with artistes including Sarkodie, Stonebwoy and Wiyaala. They have also released original songs such as “3y3 Life” and “Sanbra.” They will tell their story on JoyNews on Saturday, 15th August at 4:00 pm, with a repeat on Sunday at 10:30 am and Friday at 6:30 pm. The programme will also air on JoyPrime on Saturday, 15th August at 4:30 pm. E Vibes, the JoyNews programme that delves into the backgrounds of celebrated personalities excelling in their chosen fields, is focusing this season on music bands in Ghana. Dubbed #MusicalBandSeries, the programme celebrates the journeys, triumphs, challenges and enduring bonds of Ghanaian musical bands. The show takes viewers through the defining moments of each band’s rise, with the hope that their inspiring stories will preserve Ghana’s musical heritage and motivate the next generation.

items.title: Luca Zidane : après un Mondial 2026 décevant, le gardien des Verts rejoint Leganés
items.description: L’aventure de Luca Zidan e avec Grenade FC s’est terminée officiellement ce vendredi 7 août. Après deux saisons passées dans le club andalou et une Coupe du monde décevante avec l’Algérie, le gardien international algérien de 28 ans a signé ce vendredi à Leganés, toujours en Espagne. L’annonce a été faite par ce club qui évolue en deuxième division du championnat espagnol. « Le CD Leganés a conclu un accord ce vendredi pour la signature du gardien de but Luca Zidane Fernández, âgé de 28 ans, pour un contrat d'un an assorti d'une option pour une deuxième année », a indiqué le club dans un communiqué. Leganés ne tarit pas d’éloges sur Luca Zidane Leganés n’a pas tari d’éloge sur le fils de Zinedine Zidane. « Gardien de but doté d'une technique, de réflexes et d'un jeu au pied exceptionnels, Luca rejoint Ontime Butarque pour poursuivre sa carrière », a écrit le club de la région de Madrid, qui rappelle que le portier des Fennecs a été formé au centre de formation du Real Madrid. Luca Zidane quitte ainsi le Grenade FC après deux saisons et à l’issue d’une Coupe du monde 2026 avec l’Algérie, où il n’a pas brillé, disputant trois matchs sur quatre et encaissant six buts : trois face à l’Argentine, un contre la Jordanie et deux face à la Suisse en 16 e de finale. Il a été très critiqué par les supporters et certains anciens joueurs pour ses prestations irrégulières. Face à l’Argentine au premier tour du Mondial 2026, il lui a été reproché d’avoir encaissé un but facile à repousser. items.title: GAUA resumes nationwide strike over pay disparities
items.description: The Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) has announced the resumption of its suspended nationwide strike. The Association has directed members across Ghana’s public universities to stay away from work from Monday, August 10, until further notice over what it describes as widening pay disparities between teaching and non-teaching senior members. The decision was taken at the Association’s National Congress held in Sunyani on Friday, where delegates said recent adjustments to market premiums had created significant inequities despite teaching and non-teaching staff operating under the same analogous senior member structure. GAUA said it supports improvements in the conditions of service for teaching senior members but maintained that such gains should not come at the expense of non-teaching senior members. According to the Association, all senior members received a harmonised market premium of 114% when the Single Spine Salary Structure was introduced in 2012. Although an agreement signed with the government in April 2026 granted non-teaching senior members a 40% increase in consolidated market premium and non-basic allowances, GAUA said a substantial gap remains. The Association said teaching senior members now receive an average market premium of about GH¢10,000, compared with approximately GH¢4,718 for non-teaching senior members, a difference of about GH¢5,282. It argued that the disparity undermines fairness, internal equity and the objectives of the Single Spine Pay Policy. GAUA also expressed concern that the lowest-ranked teaching senior member, an assistant lecturer, now receives a higher market premium than the highest-ranked non-teaching senior member, such as a registrar or finance officer. The Association said it formally petitioned the National Labour Commission (NLC) and other state institutions on July 16, seeking intervention over the issue, but had not received a response. GAUA stressed that its action is not directed against teaching senior members but seeks equitable treatment for all senior members based on transparent and consistent principles. It called on the government and other stakeholders to address the disparities and uphold fairness in the remuneration of university staff. In announcing the industrial action, the Association directed all members to stay away from work until the issues in dispute are satisfactorily resolved.
