items.title: Family of Former U.S. Marine Detained in Russia Says He Is in Serious Condition
The Republic where Heroes Die while Villains Keep Digging…
items.description: On that August morning, eight Ghanaians boarded a Ghana Armed Forces helicopter expecting, like countless public servants before them, to complete another official assignment and return home before nightfall. They never did. Instead, the Republic lowered its flags. For a few solemn days, Ghana forgot its political quarrels. Radio stations softened their voices. Television presenters abandoned their usual excitement. Across the country, families mourned with families they had never met, because death has a remarkable way of reminding us that before we become NPP or NDC, ministers or soldiers, we are first fathers, husbands, brothers and friends. The men aboard that helicopter were travelling to Obuasi as part of Ghana’s continuing struggle against illegal mining. It was a journey undertaken in the service of the Republic. They paid the ultimate price. Months passed. The funerals ended. The flags were raised again. As often happens in Ghana, the headlines moved on. Then President John Mahama made a remarkable admission. Speaking about galamsey, he openly acknowledged that even members of his own political family were involved in the very enterprise his government was trying to defeat. He went further, observing that whenever governments change, many of those involved simply change political colours and continue with business as usual. It was one of those rare moments when a politician merely confirmed what the rivers have been whispering for years. Perhaps that explains why Ghana’s war against galamsey has become one of the strangest wars ever fought. Every new government arrives with bigger promises than the one before it. New task forces are inaugurated. Fresh operations are launched. Excavators are seized before television cameras. Opposition parties diagnose government failures with the confidence of Korle Bu specialists discussing somebody else’s patient. The Republic applauds. Then we quietly walk to the nearest river. The river clears its throat and delivers a different verdict. There is one institution in Ghana that no government has ever succeeded in capturing. The rivers. They have stubbornly refused to become state agencies. They do not attend ministerial briefings, applaud presidential launches or adjust their colours to suit election results. The Pra, the Birim and the Ankobra continue behaving like incorruptible public auditors, quietly examining every administration and publishing their reports in shades of brown. Rivers, it seems, are among the very few institutions in the Republic that cannot be transferred, intimidated or bribed. That is why the President’s confession deserves more than applause for honesty. If governments already know that some of their own supporters are involved in destroying our rivers, then our greatest challenge is no longer discovering the criminals. It is finding the courage to confront them. Our elders solved this puzzle long ago. They warned that anyone who spends every evening killing mosquitoes while refusing to drain the stagnant water behind the house should prepare to spend a fortune on mosquito coils. The Republic has become remarkably skilled at buying mosquito coils. We chase the young man standing waist-deep in muddy water while politely avoiding the powerful financier who purchased the excavator. We arrest the labourer but hesitate whenever the trail begins leading towards influence, wealth or political usefulness. We prune the branches with admirable enthusiasm while carefully watering the roots. That is why this debate should never become another football match between the NPP and the NDC. The previous government failed to defeat galamsey. The present government spent years explaining exactly why that failure occurred. It therefore inherited not only the responsibility of governing but also the responsibility of proving that its own diagnosis was correct. And perhaps that is the saddest lesson hidden inside that helicopter crash. A Republic should never ask its bravest citizens to risk their lives pursuing people it already knows but still struggles to confront. The greatest tribute we can pay those eight patriots is not another beautifully organised memorial service. It is ensuring that they did not sacrifice their lives merely to become another chapter in Ghana’s endless catalogue of noble intentions. History will remember the soldiers. History will remember the ministers. History will remember the public servants who never came home. The Republic must now decide whether it also wishes to remember why they boarded that helicopter. For there can be no sadder epitaph for any nation than this: Here lies a Republic where heroes died… while the villains simply kept digging. What do you think is Ghana’s biggest obstacle in defeating galamsey: political interference, corruption, poverty, weak law enforcement, or something else entirely? #StopGalamsey #SaveOurRivers #RepublicOfUncommonSense #Ghana

items.title: Lutte contre la mortalité maternelle: La SOGOB forme les sages-femmes à la prévention de l’hémorragie du post-partum
items.description: La Société des gynécologues et obstétriciens du Burkina (SOGOB) a organisé, les 6 et 7 août 2026 à Tenkodogo, un atelier de renforcement des capacités au profit des sages-femmes afin de lutter contre l’hémorragie du post-partum (HPP), l’une des principales causes de mortalité maternelle. Au Burkina Faso, environ 30 % des décès maternels sont dus à l’hémorragie du post-partum (HPP), ce qui en fait l’une des principales causes de mortalité maternelle. À travers le renforcement des capacités des acteurs de santé, la SOGOB apporte son soutien aux efforts du gouvernement en faveur de l’amélioration de la santé maternelle. Cet engagement se traduit notamment par l’adoption et la mise en œuvre de politiques ambitieuses, telles que la gratuité des soins de santé maternelle et de la planification familiale, ainsi que l’activation récente du Centre des opérations de réponse aux urgences sanitaires (CORUS), qui classe désormais les décès maternels parmi les incidents de santé, renforçant ainsi leur surveillance et la riposte. Le taux de mortalité maternelle au Burkina Faso est estimé à 198 décès pour 100 000 naissances vivantes, un niveau encore éloigné de la cible fixée par les Objectifs de développement durable (ODD), qui est de moins de 70 décès pour 100 000 naissances vivantes. Selon l’animateur de l’atelier, Pr Yobi Alexis Sawadogo, accélérer la réduction de la mortalité maternelle constitue un impératif si le Burkina Faso veut atteindre les Objectifs de développement durable. Pour y parvenir, le rôle des sage-femmes est essentiel, d’autant plus que la sensibilisation du grand public et des décideurs demeure insuffisante. Pr Yobi Alexis Sawadogo « Les sage-femmes, en tant que relais d’opinion, jouent un rôle stratégique dans la diffusion des messages de plaidoyer et la mobilisation sociale autour de cette problématique. C’est dans ce cadre que la Société des gynécologues et obstétriciens du Burkina (SOGOB) renforce leurs capacités afin d’améliorer la mobilisation communautaire et sociale autour de cette problématique », a indiqué le Pr Yobi. Durant les deux jours de formation, une trentaine de sage-femmes ont renforcé leurs capacités en matière de plaidoyer pour la réduction de la mortalité maternelle liée à l’HPP, dans le but de favoriser une meilleure couverture médiatique et une mobilisation citoyenne plus efficace. Les participantes ont également échangé sur la situation de la mortalité maternelle et de l’hémorragie du post-partum dans le monde et au Burkina Faso. À l’issue de l’atelier, les sage-femmes ont été invitées à poursuivre leur engagement dans la lutte contre l’hémorragie du post-partum, en particulier, et plus largement contre la mortalité maternelle au Burkina Faso. B.S.

items.title: Montée mensuelle des grandes couleurs : Le Manifeste de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire remis aux élèves
items.description: L'École nationale de police (ENP) a organisé, ce vendredi 7 août 2026, la traditionnelle cérémonie de montée des grandes couleurs, un moment de communion patriotique et de réaffirmation de l'engagement collectif au service de la Nation. ‎ ‎La cérémonie a été présidée par le Camarade Directeur général de l'École nationale de police, le Commissaire divisionnaire de police Abdoulaye BELEM, en présence du personnel administratif et d'encadrement, ainsi que des élèves de la 56ᵉ promotion en formation. ‎ ‎Dans son adresse, le Camarade Directeur général a salué les efforts consentis par l'ensemble du personnel dans l'accomplissement des missions assignées à l'École. Il a félicité chacun pour les résultats enregistrés et a exhorté les différents services à maintenir cette dynamique de performance, de rigueur et de professionnalisme afin de consolider davantage le rayonnement de l'école mère de la Police nationale. ‎ ‎S'inscrivant dans la vision portée par les plus hautes autorités de notre pays, le Camarade Directeur général a procédé à la remise du Manifeste de la Révolution progressiste populaire aux élèves de la 56ᵉ promotion. Il a annoncé que cet ouvrage sera également mis, dans les prochains jours, à la disposition de l'ensemble du personnel de l'École. ‎ ‎À cette occasion, il a invité le personnel et les élèves à épouser pleinement les idéaux de la Révolution progressiste populaire, fondés sur le patriotisme, l'intégrité, le sens du sacrifice, la probité, la discipline, la souveraineté nationale et le service désintéressé pour la Patrie. Il a rappelé que chaque agent de l'ENP est appelé, par son comportement et son engagement, à contribuer activement à l'édification d'une administration exemplaire au service du Burkina Faso. ‎ ‎À travers cette cérémonie, l'École nationale de police réaffirme son attachement aux valeurs de patriotisme, de discipline, de mérite et d'excellence, qui constituent le socle de la formation des femmes et des hommes appelés à assurer la sécurité des populations et la défense des institutions de la République. ‎ ‎Bien apprendre pour mieux protéger !

items.title: Mercato : Saïdou Sow fait son retour au FC Nantes
items.description: Le défenseur international guinéen Saïdou Sow retrouve le FC Nantes. Le club français a annoncé ce vendredi 7 août le retour du joueur, prêté avec option d’achat par le RC Strasbourg. Déjà passé par Nantes en janvier 2025, le défenseur central avait disputé neuf rencontres avant de voir sa saison interrompue par une grave blessure. Formé à l’AS Saint-Étienne, Saïdou Sow a ensuite rejoint Strasbourg en 2023. Après un passage au Clermont Foot la saison dernière, l’international guinéen retrouve donc les Jaune et Vert. Le FC Nantes compte désormais sur son retour pour renforcer sa défense cette saison.

items.title: «Ciné Vague Ruspina», un rendez-vous ouvert sur la mer
items.description: Du 10 au 12 août 2026, la plage de la Falaise à Monastir accueillera l'événement « Ciné Vague Ruspina ». Organisée sous l'égide du ministère des Affaires culturelles en partenariat avec le Centre national du cinéma et de l'image (CNCI). Cette manifestation se veut, durant trois jours, un rendez-vous culturel et cinématographique ouvert sur la mer, alliant art, divertissement et sensibilisation dans un espace résolument familial. Cette manifestation fait du cinéma un langage du dialogue et une fenêtre ouverte sur la réflexion. Elle met en lumière des enjeux d’actualité qui touchent l’être humain et son environnement, notamment l’importance de la préservation du milieu marin ainsi que la sensibilisation aux dangers de la migration irrégulière et aux drames et conséquences sociales et humaines qu’elle engendre. Durant trois jours, la plage de la falaise à Monastir se transformera en un espace dédié au cinéma, aux échanges, aux activités culturelles et récréatives, ainsi qu’à la rencontre entre familles et jeunes, dans une expérience qui conjugue le plaisir du spectacle et la portée du message… Là où le cinéma rencontre le bleu de la mer, la culture devient un espace de vie et d’espoir. CNCI L’article «Ciné Vague Ruspina», un rendez-vous ouvert sur la mer est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: 'Historic day': Experts, politicos weigh in on Makkah defence pact
items.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in Makkah that empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence” held at Al-Safa Palace. Since the signing, experts, political figures and commentators have offered their views on the agreement, with many describing it as a significant regional development and a historic moment for the three countries. ‘Historic day’: Attaullah Tarar Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, while talking to a private TV channel, described the signing of the joint defence agreement between the three states as a “historic day” for Pakistan, saying the pact reflected growing recognition of the country’s defence capabilities and strengthened ties among the three nations. Speaking about the agreement, Tarar said the defence cooperation framework would take relations between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to a new level. He credited Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir with bringing the three countries together, saying they had an “ideal working relationship” and that their teamwork had contributed to recent successes. An important milestone in defence cooperation: Saudi FM Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan said the pact underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries. He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity. ‘A good omen for the Muslim Ummah’: ex-minister Former federal minister Khawaja Saad Rafique took to X and hailed the agreement as “a historic development and a good omen for the Muslim Ummah”. “This agreement will prove to be a fundamental pillar for the stability, security and promotion of mutual brotherhood of the Ummah,” he wrote, praising the foresight of the three nations. ‘Welcome and timely development’ Former federal minister Mushahid Hussain called the agreement a “welcome and timely development at a crucial moment of turbulence and transformation”. In a post on X, he noted that the Makkah Agreement came soon after Pakistan’s pivotal role in brokering the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between Iran and the US, as well as the launch of the Regional 4 Diplomatic Coordination Mechanism comprising Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt. “Today’s pact has a three-fold significance. This is the first Pan-Islamic military institutional initiative among three key Muslim countries, independent of the West,” he wrote. “Second, this Muslim Defence Pact is [a] big blow to Israel and [the] ‘Abraham Accords’, as it would be an effective counter to Israeli expansionism,” Hussain added. “Third, it’s good for Pakistan’s security, given the emerging India-Israeli Axis, which has [the] backing of some regional regimes as well.” A shift beyond the US Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States. “Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States. They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.” Riyadh, in particular, he said, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war. The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, while Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he said. Step towards regional security architecture Ilhan Naz, the author of Old World Empires , took to X and called the agreement, “A positive development & another step towards a regionally owned and operated security architecture.” Culmination of regional efforts already underway Burcu Ozcelik, a Senior Fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (Rusi), called the pact the product of ongoing regional efforts and cautioned against reading into it as “evidence of a post-American Middle East”. “If anything, it fits the broader US preference for greater regional burden-sharing, regional powers assuming more responsibility for deterrence and security while remaining embedded, to different degrees, within a US-centred security architecture,” she wrote on X. “This is the culmination of regional efforts already underway. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan already have a mutual defence agreement, while Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad have spent months discussing a trilateral framework,” Ozcelik added. She noted that the signatories have their own sets of interests, priorities and existing commitments and that the agreement demonstrates a common direction. Still, the deal does not mean “unanimous consensus on all regional challenges or how to resolve them”.

items.title: GCB Bank appointed to committees for Ghana’s participation in global trade exhibitions
items.description: GCB Bank has been appointed to the National Planning Committee and several technical sub-committees overseeing Ghana’s participation in the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) 2026. The appointments, made by the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, relate to Ghana’s preparations for the international trade and investment exhibition. Under the arrangement, the Bank will chair the Budget and Fundraising Committee, co-chair the Marketing and Publicity Committee, and serve as a member of the Business and Investment Committee. According to the Ministry, the appointments were based on GCB Bank’s experience in supporting Ghana-China trade, exporter development, stakeholder engagement and previous national trade initiatives. In a related development, the Bank has nominated Aurelia Baaba Ofori Odame, Head of its State-Owned Enterprises and Afro-Asia Banking Department, to represent it on the National Planning Committee for Ghana’s participation in the China International Import Expo 2026, the Specialised World Expo 2027 in Belgrade, Serbia, and the Green X Expo 2027 in Yokohama, Japan. The committees are expected to coordinate Ghana’s participation in the exhibitions, which are aimed at promoting trade, investment and international business partnerships. Commenting on the appointments, Ms Ofori Odame said they reflected the Bank’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s international trade objectives. “We are honoured by the confidence the Ministry has reposed in GCB Bank. These appointments affirm our commitment to facilitating cross-border trade and creating opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to access international markets. Through our specialised Afro-Asia Banking Department, we have consistently worked to connect businesses with strategic markets, particularly in Asia, and we look forward to contributing to Ghana’s participation in these global platforms,” she said. She added that international exhibitions such as the China International Import Expo and the World Expo provide opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to engage with buyers, investors and strategic partners while expanding their presence in international markets. GCB Bank says it has expanded its support for international trade in recent years through its Africa and Asia Corridor strategy by providing financial services, facilitating business partnerships and supporting exporters seeking access to regional and international markets.

items.title: Spear Institute calls for overhaul of Ghana’s flood management system to prevent recurring disasters
items.description: Spear Institute has called for a major overhaul of Ghana’s flood management approach, urging authorities to shift from responding to disasters after they occur to investing in long-term prevention and climate resilience. The research firm made the call during a virtual media briefing on Friday, August 7, 2026, where it examined the country’s recurring flood crisis and proposed measures to reduce its impact. The session, themed “Flooding in Ghana: Paddling to Safety or Avoiding a Repeat,” analysed the causes and consequences of flooding through four areas: socioeconomic conditions, governance, engineering and infrastructure, and project management. According to Spear Institute, flooding has been a recurring challenge in Ghana for decades, but the growing impact on lives, businesses, infrastructure and livelihoods requires a more coordinated national response. Using the June 29, 2026 floods in Accra as a case study, the institute said the disaster exposed weaknesses in drainage systems, land-use planning and disaster preparedness. It said the floods led to major disruptions, including impassable roads, flooded homes and businesses, and interruptions to transport and commercial activities. The institute reported that more than 12 people lost their lives, seven were missing, and 7,761 households were displaced across 18 affected assemblies following the incident. Spear Institute identified climate change, rapid urbanisation and the destruction of natural flood-control systems such as wetlands as key factors worsening the impact and frequency of floods. It noted that increasing population growth and unplanned development are placing additional pressure on vulnerable areas. The research firm stressed that flooding is a complex challenge that cannot be addressed by one sector alone, requiring coordinated action across government, communities and private stakeholders. On the social and economic dimensions of flooding, Spear Institute said poverty and inequality often increase exposure to flood risks. It explained that some low-income households occupy flood-prone areas due to limited access to affordable and safer housing options. The institute also warned that households and small businesses without insurance, savings or access to credit often struggle to recover after losing property, equipment and sources of income. While identifying indiscriminate waste disposal as a contributor to blocked drains and waterways, the institute cautioned against placing the entire responsibility on citizens. It called for stronger waste management systems, including reliable collection services, accessible disposal facilities, enforcement and sustained public education. Spear Institute’s engineering and infrastructure team argued that Accra’s drainage systems must be reassessed and redesigned to reflect current population levels, urban expansion and changing rainfall patterns. It said the city recorded about 169.23 millimetres of rainfall during the June 29 floods, a volume that exceeded the capacity of some existing drainage infrastructure. The institute noted that several drains, culverts and bridges were constructed decades ago and no longer adequately serve today’s urban environment. It also raised concerns about the narrowing of waterways, including the Koli Lagoon and Odora River, due to encroachment, land reclamation and waste disposal. “When water loses its path, it creates another path,” one of the presenters said, highlighting the consequences of obstructed waterways. The institute further called for improved waste management, arguing that investments in drainage infrastructure would have limited impact if drains remain clogged with waste. Spear Institute also criticised weaknesses in project management, including inadequate attention to sustainability, quality control and stakeholder involvement. It argued that infrastructure projects should not be judged only by whether they are completed on time and within budget. Instead, projects must also be assessed on their ability to withstand future climate conditions and protect communities over time. The research firm criticised Ghana’s largely reactive approach to flooding, citing emergency interventions such as relief funding and nationwide de-silting exercises as responses that come after disasters occur. While acknowledging the importance of such interventions, Spear Institute said they do not address the underlying causes of flooding. It is calling for greater investment in proactive measures, including improved urban planning, restoration of wetlands, sustainable drainage systems and stronger flood-resilience strategies. The institute believes Ghana’s flood challenge requires an integrated national approach that combines engineering solutions with social protection, effective governance and better project management. It said the goal should be to develop systems capable of withstanding changing environmental conditions rather than repeatedly responding after floods strike. For Ghana, Spear Institute argues, the priority must now move from managing the aftermath of floods to preparing communities and cities before the next rainfall disaster occurs.

items.title: DPBEP 2027- 2029 : une consolidation budgétaire résolue, sans austérité
items.description: Le retour à la soutenabilité des finances publiques constitue le fil conducteur du Document de Programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027- 2029. Le gouvernement inscrit le déficit dans une trajectoire de réduction continue : 4,9% du PIB en 2027, 3,8% en 2028, puis 3,0% en 2029, conformément à la norme communautaire de l'Union économique et monétaire ouest africaine (UEMOA). Le Document de Programmation budgétaire et économique pluriannuelle (DPBEP) 2027- 2029 montre que sur l'ensemble du triennat, les recettes de la loi de finances atteignent 19 228 milliards FCFA et les dépenses 22 133 milliards. Pour les recettes du budget général, elles progressant de 716 milliards quand les dépenses ne s'accroissent que de 350 milliards. A lire aussi : Finances publiques : les recettes de l’État estimées à 427,9 milliards de FCFA en mai 2026 « Cet ajustement repose sur une logique claire : rationaliser ce qui ne transforme pas, investir dans ce qui transforme. Les dépenses courantes reculent de 159 milliards FCFA sur la période, à la faveur de la maîtrise de la masse salariale, dont le ratio sur les recettes fiscales demeure sous le seuil de 35%, et de la rationalisation des subventions et transferts au secteur parapublic », indique le document. Dans le même temps, souligne la même source, les dépenses d'investissement progressent de 510 milliards FCFA, orientées vers les projets à fort impact économique et social. « Du côté des recettes, la pression fiscale franchira pour la première fois le seuil communautaire de 20%, pour s'établir à 21% dès 2027, grâce à une Stratégie de Recettes à Moyen Terme privilégiant l'élargissement de l'assiette, intégration du secteur informel, fiscalité foncière, taxation de l'économie numérique, sur le relèvement des taux », lit-on dans le texte. 4 326,3 milliards de dépenses courantes Il ressort aussi de ce document que les dépenses courantes, se situeraient à 4 326,3 milliards FCFA en 2029 contre 4 485,7 milliards FCFA en 2027. Pour les intérêts sur la dette publique, elles seraient payés à hauteur de 1 303,9 milliards FCFA en 2027 à 1 061,4 milliards FCFA en 2029. Il convient de noter aussi de noter que les charges sont projetées à 22 132,7 milliards FCFA et les prévisions de ressources sont attendues à 6 082,1 milliards FCFA. Quant aux dépenses, elles sont prévues à hauteur de 7 242,3 milliards FCFA. Ce qui laisse un déficit budgétaire 1 160,3 milliards FCFA. Concernant le Produit intérieur brut (PIB) nominal, il est évalué à 23 672,8 milliards FCFA. Les recettes du budget général sont projetées globalement sur la période triennale à 18 286,0 milliards FCFA constituées de recettes internes de 17 654,8 milliards FCFA et des recettes externes de 631,2 milliards FCFA. 5 527,0 milliards FCFA de recettes internes en 2027 Par rapport aux recettes internes, elles passent de 5 527,0 milliards FCFA en 2027 à 6 224,2 milliards FCFA en 2029. Les ressources externes, elles passeraient de 201,4 milliards FCFA à 220,2 milliards FCFA Pour les transferts courants y compris les subventions à différents secteurs passeraient de 1 220,3 milliards FCFA en 2027 à 1 195 milliards FCFA en 2029. Le document informe également que le besoin global de financement de l’économie estimé à 19 689,4 milliards FCFA et les Comptes Spéciaux du Trésor sont évalués à 941,9 milliards FCFA pendant cette période. Il urge aussi de souligner qu’en 2029, les recettes et dépenses des collectivités territoriales dotées de ressources propres avoisineront respectivement 389,3 milliards FCFA et 275,2 milliards FCFA. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Goods transporters to go on strike from Saturday after talks with govt fail
items.description: Goods transporters and oil tanker operators began suspending their services on Friday night after negotiations with the government failed, ahead of their nationwide wheel-jam strike scheduled for Saturday. All Pakistan Goods Transport Itehad spokesman and All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Mohammad Owais Chaudhry Advocate told Dawn that talks with Federal Minister for Communications Aleem Khan and other government officials had failed. He said the negotiations ended without a breakthrough, prompting transporters, including edible oil tanker operators, petroleum oil tanker operators, truckers, trailer operators and other intercity transporters, to proceed with their previously announced strike. “We have informed the government side about the problems we are facing and our concerns,” Chaudhry said, adding that the strike would continue until their demands were accepted. However, the minister has assured the transporters that he would discuss their demands, and the next round of talks would be held on Monday morning. The unified body of transporters had already announced that it would begin its wheel-jam strike from August 8, and warned that it would not be a token strike but an indefinite one. “Commercial goods carriers across the country have already been taken off the roads and will remain stationed at designated places during the protest period,” Chaudhry said. Among the key demands of the transporters is the uniform enforcement of axle-load limits across the country and permission for 10-wheel vehicles to carry up to 35 tonnes. They have also demanded reductions in diesel prices and toll taxes, besides seeking relief in withholding tax to ease the financial burden on the transport sector. The transporters have also called for the withdrawal of customs provisions that, according to the association, allow authorities to confiscate vehicles carrying goods found to be in violation of customs laws. Other demands include the withdrawal of the Punjab Highway Patrol’s powers to issue challans to commercial vehicles, an end to what the association described as unnecessary challans and excessive fines on motorways and highways, and measures to facilitate the issuance of heavy transport vehicle licences to drivers.

items.title: Vasty Arthur takes Tinsel Couture and Ghana’s Northern heritage to the global runway
items.description: Ghanaian fashion designer Vasty Arthur, Creative Director of Tinsel Couture, has taken the richness of Ghanaian culture to the international stage, presenting a striking collection inspired by Northern Ghana’s textile heritage at an international runway event in Kazan, Republic of Tatarstan, Russia. Through her collection, The Pride of the North, Vasty used fashion to tell a distinctly Ghanaian story rooted in craftsmanship, identity and the generations of artisans who have preserved the country’s traditional textile heritage. The collection was showcased at the 5th International Ethno-Fashion Festival “Lifestyle – Cultural Code,” an international gathering of designers, artisans, cultural leaders and fashion enthusiasts that celebrates fashion as an expression of living culture. For Vasty and Tinsel Couture, the event represented more than a fashion showcase. It was an opportunity to present Ghanaian design and craftsmanship to a global audience while demonstrating how traditional textiles can be transformed into contemporary fashion with international appeal From Northern Ghana to the World At the heart of The Pride of the North is one of Northern Ghana’s most recognisable cultural symbols—the traditional smock, popularly known as the fugu or batakari. Handwoven in narrow strips and carefully stitched together, the smock represents generations of craftsmanship, patience, resilience and community. Rather than reproducing traditional garments, Vasty Arthur reinterpreted the textile for the modern runway, combining its distinctive textures and cultural significance with contemporary silhouettes and refined tailoring. The result is a collection that remains unmistakably Ghanaian while demonstrating that indigenous textiles have a place in modern international fashion. This approach reflects the philosophy behind Tinsel Couture: preserving heritage while reimagining it for contemporary audiences. Under Vasty’s creative direction, traditional craftsmanship serves as a foundation for innovation, celebrating Ghana’s rich fashion heritage while exploring new possibilities. Fashion as Cultural Storytelling For Tinsel Couture, fashion is more than clothing—it is a medium for telling stories and celebrating identity. In The Pride of the North, the Northern smock is complemented by handwoven Kente and traditional tie-dye fabrics, bringing together some of Ghana’s most iconic textile traditions in a single contemporary collection. Kente, long associated with royalty, achievement, wisdom and identity, adds another layer of cultural symbolism, while the tie-dye fabrics highlight the creativity and individuality of Ghanaian artisans. Rather than allowing these textiles to compete, Vasty blends them into a cohesive visual narrative that reflects Ghana’s cultural diversity and shared national identity. The collection avoids turning traditional attire into costume. Instead, its modern silhouettes, thoughtful tailoring and wearable designs allow heritage to inspire fashion that speaks confidently to contemporary audiences. Designing with Purpose At the centre of this creative journey is Vasty Arthur, whose work continues to demonstrate the ability of Ghanaian designers to transform indigenous knowledge into fashion that resonates both locally and internationally. Her presentation in Kazan placed her alongside designers representing cultures from around the world. It also provided an opportunity to showcase Ghana through the skill of its artisans, the richness of its textiles and the creativity of its contemporary fashion industry. Each garment reflects the work of the people behind the fabric—from the weavers who preserve centuries-old techniques to the artisans whose craftsmanship remains central to Ghana’s cultural identity. By bringing their work to an international runway, Vasty Arthur and Tinsel Couture helped introduce these traditions to a wider global audience. Weaving Heritage into the Future An old Northern Ghanaian proverb says, “A single strand cannot weave a smock.” The saying speaks to collaboration, community and the many hands required to create something enduring. It also reflects the essence of The Pride of the North. Behind every garment is a chain of cultural knowledge—from those who spin and weave the threads to the artisans who preserve traditional techniques and the designer who reimagines them for a contemporary audience. Through Tinsel Couture, Vasty Arthur demonstrates that Ghanaian heritage need not be abandoned in pursuit of global relevance. Instead, it can serve as a source of creativity and innovation. Her appearance in Kazan was therefore more than a runway presentation. It celebrated Ghanaian creativity, honoured the artisans who continue to sustain the country’s textile traditions and reaffirmed the growing place of African fashion on the global stage. With The Pride of the North, Vasty Arthur and Tinsel Couture are not simply preserving Ghana’s textile heritage—they are reimagining it for a new generation and weaving it confidently into the future of global fashion.

items.title: What is the Patriot missile system and why are supplies depleted worldwide?
items.description: First used in the 1991 Gulf War, the US Patriot air defence system has seen demand spike sharply this year, with supplies of interceptor missiles depleted by Ukraine’s war against the Russian invasion and the widening war in the Middle East. Ukraine is urgently seeking more Patriot interceptors to defend against a nightly barrage of Russian ballistic missile strikes. But the Iran war has drained arsenals in the US and the Gulf, and some European countries are holding onto missiles they may need for their own defence. The following are some details about the Patriot air defence system, one of the most advanced weapons in the US arsenal. What is the Patriot system? Patriot, short for Phased Array Tracking Radar for Intercept on Target, is a mobile surface-to-air missile defence system built by US weapons maker Raytheon Technologies that can be used in all kinds of weather and at long range. Developed in the 1980s, the Patriot system has been modernised over the past decades, expanding its capabilities and reach. It is slated to remain in service through 2048. A typical battery includes radar and control systems, a power unit, launchers, and support vehicles. The system can intercept aircraft, tactical ballistic missiles and cruise missiles, depending on the interceptor used. What can the Patriot system do? The system has different capabilities depending on the type of interceptor used. The earlier PAC-2 interceptor uses a blast-fragmentation warhead that detonates in the vicinity of a target, while the PAC-3 family of missiles uses more accurate “hit-to-kill” technology to physically collide with the target. Raytheon makes the PAC-2 GEM-T interceptor, which can defeat smaller, short-range ballistic missiles, cruise missiles or enemy aircraft. Lockheed Martin, the world’s largest arms maker, builds the more advanced PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE), which can hit longer-range ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, aircraft and also hypersonics. In July, Lockheed introduced a new interceptor, the PAC-3 Adapted Capability Effector (ACE), which it says will cost half as much while still being able to target short-range ballistic missiles, aircraft and cruise missiles. The system’s radar has a range of over 150 kilometres and can simultaneously track up to 100 potential targets, the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (Nato) said in 2015. Although not originally designed to intercept hypersonic weapons, in May 2023 the US confirmed Ukraine had used the Patriot system to shoot down a Russian Kinzhal missile, which Moscow claims is hypersonic. Countries closely guard details about the number of targets destroyed by Patriot systems, although Ukraine said in January it had destroyed 250 targets, including 140 ballistic missiles. Patriot has also destroyed dozens of Iranian ballistic missiles in the Gulf, although details have not been released. How widely is it used? Raytheon has built and delivered over 240 Patriot fire units, according to its website. Raytheon and Lockheed together have manufactured thousands of interceptor missiles. Nineteen countries now operate the Patriot system, according to Raytheon, including the US, Germany, Poland, Ukraine, Japan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Egypt. Of these countries, 16 have the newest PAC-3 MSE missiles, while six to eight countries have requested additional missiles to replenish their depleted stocks. In this US Army handout photo released on June 1, 2026, a US Army air defence artilleryman conducts maintenance on an MIM-104 Patriot missile system, the army’s primary terminal-phase anti-ballistic missile system, at an undisclosed location in the Middle East. — AFP/File How much does it cost? A newly produced single Patriot battery costs over $1 billion, including $400 million for the system and $690m for the missiles in a battery, according to the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). Patriot PAC-3 interceptors are estimated at around $4m to $5m per missile. Why are supplies dwindling? Specific inventory numbers are classified, but CSIS estimates that about 65 per cent of US Patriot interceptors were expended between February and July, with less than 850 left on hand, down from 2,330 before the Iran war began. Current inventories in the Gulf states are also severely depleted, and several European countries have transferred some of their supplies to Ukraine , experts say. Saudi Arabia used about 86pc of its 2,800 PAC-3 interceptors in the first 38 days of combat, leaving it with 400 missiles left in April. Other Gulf nations used up similar amounts of their inventories, CSIS said. Are countries buying more Patriots to boost inventories? The US has approved the sale of 5,250 interceptors to Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates for replenishment. The US is also pressing ahead with talks on allowing Ukraine to make Patriot interceptor missiles, even after President Donald Trump cast doubt on such a deal, sources familiar with the discussions said. The talks include an option for Ukraine to build some components for final assembly elsewhere in Europe. Last month, the US Army awarded Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6bn to produce Patriot interceptor missiles.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Une nouvelle centrale thermique de 26,4 MW renforce les capacités de production d’électricité
items.description: Le Burkina Faso poursuit le renforcement de son autonomie énergétique. Le ministre de l'Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, a officiellement mis en service, ce 7 août 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, la nouvelle centrale thermique de Bobo II d'une capacité de 26,4 MW. Réalisée en 15 mois pour un investissement de plus de 33 milliards de FCFA, cette infrastructure énergétique permet de porter la capacité totale de la centrale de Bobo II de 60 MW à 86,4 MW et marque une nouvelle étape dans la politique gouvernementale de consolidation de l'offre nationale d'électricité. Elle permet également au Burkina Faso de franchir une nouvelle étape dans sa stratégie de renforcement de la production nationale d'électricité. La nouvelle centrale est équipée de trois groupes électrogènes de dernière génération développant chacun une puissance de 8,8 MW Selon le directeur général de la SONABEL, Souleymane Ouédraogo, la nouvelle centrale est équipée de trois groupes électrogènes de dernière génération développant chacun une puissance de 8,8 MW, soit une capacité totale installée de 26,4 MW. L'installation fonctionne principalement au fuel lourd, tandis que le diesel est utilisé pour le démarrage des moteurs et comme combustible de secours. Pour le ministre Yacouba Zabré Gouba, cette réalisation répond à une ambition claire qui celle d’accroître les capacités nationales de production, réduire progressivement la dépendance du Burkina Faso aux importations d'énergie et garantir un approvisionnement plus stable aux populations et aux entreprises. Pour lui, la centrale constitue alors un investissement stratégique pour le pays. Elle permettra de renforcer durablement le système électrique tout en accompagnant le développement économique et industriel. Le projet a été réalisé en 15 mois au lieu de 24 mois comme prévu L'électricité produite par cette infrastructure sera injectée dans le Réseau national interconnecté (RNI), permettant ainsi d'améliorer la qualité et la disponibilité de l'énergie électrique sur l'ensemble du territoire. Le ministre a également salué la performance des équipes techniques ayant conduit le projet. Alors que les travaux étaient programmés pour une durée de 24 mois, la centrale a été réalisée en seulement 15 mois, soit neuf mois avant l'échéance initiale. Une prouesse qui permettra d'accroître plus rapidement les capacités nationales de production dans un contexte où la demande en électricité ne cesse de croître. La centrale de Bobo II traduit la volonté des autorités burkinabè d'investir dans des infrastructures structurantes Cette nouvelle centrale s'inscrit dans le vaste programme gouvernemental de développement des infrastructures énergétiques, engagé afin de renforcer la souveraineté énergétique du Burkina Faso. Après la mise en service de la centrale thermique de Pabré le 21 juillet dernier, le gouvernement entend poursuivre cette dynamique avec l'entrée en exploitation prochaine des centrales thermiques de Koudougou et de Kaya, d'une capacité de 25 MW chacune. Ces nouvelles infrastructures viendront renforcer davantage le parc national de production et contribuer à sécuriser l'alimentation électrique du pays. Au-delà des chiffres, la mise en service de la centrale de Bobo II traduit la volonté des autorités burkinabè d'investir dans des infrastructures structurantes capables de soutenir la croissance économique, d'améliorer la compétitivité des entreprises et d'offrir aux populations un meilleur accès à une électricité fiable. items.title: Fête de l'indépendance de la Côte d'Ivoire : Alassane Ouattara prône «l'unité, le travail et la discipline»
items.description: Dans son traditionnel discours a la nation, le 6 août, a la veille du 66ᵉ anniversaire de l'accession de la Cote d'Ivoire a l'independance, le president Alassane Ouattara a adresse ses hommages aux Forces de defense et de securite et aux forces vives du pays pour leur contribution a la paix et la securite, ainsi qu'au progres du pays. Le chef de l'etat a aussi estime que les ambitions de son pays reposent sur des valeurs telles que « l'unite, le travail, la discipline, la solidarite et la confiance », appelant les citoyens a contribuer au developpement economique et social de la Cote d'Ivoire. Défilé des forces spéciales de Côte d'Ivoire 🇨🇮. Bonne fête de l’indépendance au peuple ivoiriens 🇨🇮 💪 pic.twitter.com/TZSmyPIh9j — Said_du_Mali🇲🇱🇫🇷🔥✌🏽 (@Said_du_Mali) August 7, 2026 Retour sur les defis qui s'imposent a la Cote d'Ivoire Rappelant le contexte mondial marque par les incertitudes, les tensions geopolitiques, les defis securitaires, les consequences d'un climat qui change et un environnement economique mondial fragile, le president ivoirien a evoque les pluies torrentielles et les inondations qui ont sinistre des regions du pays. Exprimant ses condoleances aux familles des victimes et sa compassion aux populations lesees, il a fait part de la determination du gouvernement pour accelerer « les investissements dans les infrastructures de drainage et d'assainissement, renforcer les dispositifs de prevention et poursuivre les programmes de logements sociaux ». 🇨🇮 ✌🏽🥷Fête de l'indépendance de la Côte d'Ivoire : la Gendarmerie nationale lors du défilé officiel. pic.twitter.com/EdJivSiWjU — Said_du_Mali🇲🇱🇫🇷🔥✌🏽 (@Said_du_Mali) August 7, 2026 Sur le plan securitaire, Alassane Ouattara a egalement annonce la poursuite des « operations de liberation des zones a risque », et ce, « dans le strict respect de l'etat de droit, pour preserver des vies humaines ». #Indépendance2025 Le Président de la République, Alassane Ouattara, a présidé, ce jeudi 7 août 2025, la cérémonie commémorative du 65e anniversaire de l'indépendance de la Côte d’Ivoire, marquée par un défilé militaire et une parade carnavalesque. pic.twitter.com/hph0hz2emS — Presidenceci (@Presidenceci) August 7, 2025 Le cap du developpement est maintenu et l'economie reste « dynamique » En matiere economique, le president ivoirien a affirme que son pays a « su maintenir sa trajectoire de developpement ». Il a egalement indique un dynamisme de l'economie nationale, assurant que la Cote d'Ivoire disposait d'un taux de croissance annuel des « plus eleves de la region et du monde, confirmant la solidite de ses fondamentaux ». Il s'est engage dans ce contexte a poursuivre les efforts pour renforcer les acces a l'eau potable, a l'electricite, aux soins de sante, a une education de qualite, au logement et a des services publics toujours plus performants. Il a aussi souligne l'engagement de son gouvernement pour ameliorer la situation de l'emploi, du pouvoir d'achat et pour proteger les plus vulnerables. À vous, #femmes et #hommes qui travaillez la #terre ivoirienne : merci. Ce vendredi, à #Yopougon , notre pays a célébré ses 66 ans d'indépendance aux côtés du Président @AOuattara_PRCI . Parmi les temps forts : un hommage à l' #agriculture ivoirienne, à travers de beaux tableaux… pic.twitter.com/oV2tCxJ58B — Bruno Nabagné KONÉ (@Bruno_N_Kone) August 7, 2026 Grâce presidentielle pour 4 661 detenus de droit commun Alassane Ouattara a signe deux decrets au titre de la Justice. Un premier accordant la grâce presidentielle a 2 064 detenus, alors que le second stipule une remise de peine a 2 597 detenus dont le reliquat de la peine est inferieur a trente-six mois. Les deux textes combines accordent donc la liberte a 4 661 detenus de droit commun, condamnes pour des infractions mineures.

items.title: The Internet Is in Crisis
items.description: Almost 20 years ago, I had tickets to see Amy Winehouse perform in London, at a show that was canceled just an hour before it was scheduled to start. A friend and I went to a nearby hotel bar instead, and not much later, in walked Winehouse herself—tiny, grubby, and completely incoherent. She walked over to us and stared, her eyes both furious and vacant, until someone in her entourage came and dragged her away. I remember the person who flashed to mind in that bizarre moment: the gossip blogger Perez Hilton. If you weren’t regularly online during the late 2000s, it’s hard to explain how dominant a presence Hilton was—how incessantly he posted about what celebrities might be doing on any given day, how shameless he was about posting upskirt photos, how judgmental his tirades about young women in crisis were. His fiendish MO was lifting pictures from paparazzi agencies and then scribbling penises or obscene epithets on them in order to claim fair use. Hilton—whose real name is Mario Lavandeira Jr.—was particularly cruel about Winehouse, who was being photographed by the celebrity press almost daily in states of disarray. He posted, by turns, about her physical appearance (“super skinny, dirty and wasted”), false rumors of her pregnancy (“We were sure that her ovaries were too gin-soaked to be of any use”), and a performance in which she wasn’t wearing underwear (“Grrrossss!!!!!!!!! Who needs to see cracked out snatch?”). PerezHilton.com was relentless and brutal, and its readers could not get enough, especially when the blog’s coverage collided with moments of calamitous celebrity breakdown. (When the actor Lindsay Lohan was arrested in 2007, the site reportedly received 8.8 million pageviews that day.) Since then, the internet has metastasized into something officially kinder—we no longer berate famous people in crisis for sport quite as much as we used to—and quietly more appalling, where irony-poisoned young men broadcast their executions and social-media companies seem to basically shrug in response. And so, on Tuesday night, during what seemed to be a mental-health breakdown of his own, Hilton was able to stream himself live on TikTok cutting himself with a knife for about 15 minutes before his broadcast was finally interrupted. Any number of Hilton’s followers on TikTok could have clicked on the stream thinking they were going to see a standard broadcast about Ariana Grande or Trader Joe’s ready meals (both of which Hilton had posted about on YouTube in recent weeks). Instead, they got a scene of unimaginable violence. “I am fine with horror/gore, have seen a lot real and fake, and this was so deeply disturbing I could not get the image out of my head all night,” one commenter posted on Reddit . Another added, “I watch cartel torture and beheading videos with no issues. I had to turn the perez video off after about 20 seconds, and I felt deeply disturbed for hours.” TikTok’s failure to interrupt Hilton’s broadcast for such a long time, even as horrified viewers were reporting it, is astonishing. (A spokesperson for the site told Wired that a “moderator error” caused a delay in removal; another told Vanity Fair that Hilton was persistent in his attempts to broadcast what he was doing, using several different streams to do so.) [ Read: The unspeakable, enabled ] In the United States, Section 230 of the Communications Act shields technology and communication companies from being held legally responsible for third-party content that appears on their platforms. And since Facebook launched livestreaming in 2015, social-media sites have struggled to establish safeguards for atrocities being broadcast in real time, to the point where the phenomenon of people livestreaming their own attempts to die has become “ an emerging public health crisis ,” in the words of psychology researchers. After a man livestreamed himself killing 51 people at two mosques in New Zealand in 2019 on Facebook Live, Facebook said it was investing in “technical innovation” to prevent people from abusing its platform. Nevertheless, footage of mass shootings and other atrocities proliferates globally before befuddled tech companies can tie their shoes. The tone of the contemporary internet is also darker and more nihilist than it has ever been. “Social-media platforms—and especially X—have loosened their grip on moderation at the same time that AI tools have allowed for the easy proliferation of slop,” my colleague Charlie Warzel wrote earlier this year. “Never before has there been so much cynical, cruel content and trolling.” But the idea that Hilton might end up turning self-harm into content feels particularly fraught. A statement from his family posted online said that the influencer had been “experiencing a severe mental-health crisis,” and that his three children, his niece, and his sister were at home with Hilton when he began hurting himself, although they left immediately “to protect the children from witnessing any further trauma.” Over the past decade and a half, Hilton has tried to pivot away from the bilious celebrity coverage that made him so successful: In a 2010 video, he announced that he would no longer be cruel. But his popularity never quite recovered, and he argued in his 2020 memoir, TMI , that the toxicity of his site was what had appealed to his readers, even if they didn’t want to admit it to themselves: “The more snarky names I gave the celebrities, the more penises or coke or boogers I drew on pictures of them, the more people visited my page.” It’s also true that PerezHilton.com peaked in its cultural relevance around 2007, the year that celebrity after celebrity seemed to be breaking down in public while pursued by paparazzi on mopeds. That year, Britney Spears shaved her head (when the actor Heath Ledger died in 2008, Hilton sold T-shirts emblazoned with the words Why Couldn’t It Be Britney? ), Anna-Nicole Smith overdosed on prescription medication, Lohan was arrested for cocaine possession, Paris Hilton went to jail, and Mischa Barton was arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol. Hilton documented each of these moments in vivid and elaborate detail—my browser finally quit when I got to page 79 of his archives related to Amy Winehouse—because he understood what people wanted from him and his work. “When Britney Spears was at her wildest, people were glued to my website,” he wrote in TMI. It’s impossible to know whether this awareness informed what he did to himself this week, and how he did it. Hilton’s breakdown is desperately sad; I’m haunted by the idea of what his children might have seen happen in their home, but also by the idea of what all children might see, at any time, in this hopelessly corrupted and seemingly unsalvageable internet. If you are having thoughts of suicide, please know that you are not alone. If you are in danger of acting on suicidal thoughts, call 911. For support and resources, call the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988 or text 741-741 for the Crisis Text Line.

items.title: The Case for Calling People on the Phone
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. Conversation has become optimized—but not always for the better. We send a quick text instead of making a call, react with an emoji instead of a laugh, and turn catching up into a series of efficient updates. Although staying in touch with people is easier than ever, we spend surprisingly little time talking to one another. “No one picks up the phone anymore,” Alexis C. Madrigal wrote in 2018. That’s in part because too many faceless telemarketers have our number, and in part because more people have come to treat phone calls as something to reserve for emergencies or bad news or major life events. However, in many cases they’re the easiest way to have conversations that texting can’t quite convey—ones that meander, surprise you, and leave you feeling a little more connected than before. Texting has made communication faster and more efficient, but not necessarily more conversational. Today’s newsletter is a reminder that you don’t need a reason or an agenda to call someone you’ve been thinking about. On Conversation Talk to People on the Telephone By Amanda Mull It’s time to start calling your friends again. ( From 2019 ) Read the article. Why No One Answers Their Phone Anymore By Alexis C. Madrigal Telephone culture is disappearing. ( From 2018 ) Read the article. Another Symptom of Growing Isolation By Olga Khazan A recent study found that people spoke fewer words a day in 2019 than in 2005. Read the article. Still Curious? The tension that defines modern life : Most people have a smartphone. But many want to use it less, Julie Beck writes. Maybe don’t send that voice note . The audio messages can encourage selfishness—unless you use them gracefully, Jacob Sweet argued in 2024. Other Diversions Bring back the blue-book exam. The dishonesty of true crime The new parent trap PS Courtesy of Bonnie B. My colleague Isabel Fattal recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. “My sense of awe for this world comes from my backyard, where a family of barred owls nests each year and produces angelic chicks that begin their lives playing among the trees,” Bonnie B. from Cordova, Tennessee, shared. “They make me believe in the magic of life.” We’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Rafaela

items.description: L'Administration pénitentiaire poursuit sa politique de réinsertion sociale et professionnelle des personnes privées de liberté. Trente détenus mineurs de la Maison d'Arrêt et de Correction (MAC) de Hann bénéficient actuellement d'une formation professionnelle en plomberie, financée par le Fonds de Financement de la Formation Professionnelle et Technique (3FPT). D'une durée de trois mois, le programme combine apprentissages théoriques et pratiques : installation, entretien et réparation des équipements et réseaux sanitaires. À l'issue de la formation, les bénéficiaires disposeront d'une qualification directement mobilisable sur le marché du travail un secteur où la demande de main-d'œuvre qualifiée reste forte au Sénégal. Un pari sur l'avenir des jeunes détenus Au-delà du geste technique, c'est une logique de réinsertion durable que l'Administration pénitentiaire entend consolider. En misant sur la formation plutôt que sur la seule sanction, l'institution cherche à offrir à ces jeunes détenus des outils concrets d'autonomie, susceptibles de faciliter leur retour à la vie active une fois leur peine purgée. Cette démarche s'inscrit dans une approche plus large de prévention de la récidive, où l'investissement dans les compétences devient un levier d'inclusion socio-économique. Pour l'Administration pénitentiaire, chaque parcours de formation réussi représente un pas de plus vers une sortie de détention mieux préparée et une chance supplémentaire donnée à ces mineurs de se reconstruire. C.G.D

Burkina Faso : Farakan Labs lance PengMe, une plateforme pour faciliter l’avance sur salaire en cas d’urgence
items.description: La startup studio burkinabè Farakan Labs a officiellement lancé, ce 7 août 2026 à Ouagadougou, PengMe (« Prête-moi » en mooré), une plateforme numérique destinée à rapprocher les particuliers et les entreprises de solutions de financement d'urgence. Premier service proposé : une avance sur salaire digitalisée, accessible via une application mobile. Face aux difficultés que rencontrent de nombreux travailleurs pour accéder rapidement à des liquidités en cas d'imprévu, Farakan Labs propose une réponse numérique avec PengMe . Disponible sur les plateformes de téléchargement d'applications mobiles, cette solution ambitionne de simplifier les démarches d'avance sur salaire, notamment pour les salariés non bancarisés qui perçoivent néanmoins des revenus réguliers. Pour illustrer l'intérêt de cette innovation, Jérôme Kaboré, cofondateur de Farakan Labs, évoque le cas d'un salarié payé en espèces dont l'enfant tombe malade en soirée, alors qu'aucun responsable des ressources humaines n'est disponible pour traiter une demande d'avance sur salaire. « L'urgence financière ne prévient pas », résume-t-il. Selon lui, un salarié disposant d'un revenu régulier ne devrait pas être contraint de solliciter ses proches pour faire face à une dépense urgente. Le fonctionnement de PengMe place les entreprises au cœur du dispositif. Celles-ci souscrivent à la plateforme et déterminent les règles d'utilisation : ouverture des périodes d'avance sur salaire, fixation des plafonds, validation des employés éligibles et supervision du processus. Les salariés concernés créent ensuite leur compte personnel, relié à celui de leur entreprise. Après les vérifications d'identité, ils peuvent soumettre leurs demandes directement depuis l'application, dans les limites définies par leur employeur. Une fois la demande validée par les partenaires financiers de PengMe, les fonds sont transférés électroniquement. Le remboursement est ensuite effectué par l’employeur au moment du paiement des salaires. « À la fin du mois, on sait que c'est le responsable de la paie qui verse les salaires. Comme lui a accès à la plateforme, une facture lui est envoyée et c'est lui qui fait le virement sur le compte qu'on aura assigné », explique Jérôme Kaboré. Lors de la démonstration technique, le cofondateur et directeur technique de Farakan Labs, Irmeya Ouédraogo, a précisé que le plafond actuel est fixé à 50 000 FCFA , avec une limite correspondant au quart du salaire du bénéficiaire. Ces paramètres pourront évoluer au fur et à mesure du développement de la plateforme. « Nous ne sommes pas une institution financière. Nous sommes en discussion avec les institutions financières qui vont porter, derrière, cette initiative. Nous sommes l'interface que l'utilisateur utilise pour communiquer avec ces institutions », a-t-il souligné. Pour cette phase de lancement, l'utilisation de PengMe est gratuite pour les entreprises qui souhaitent adhérer au service. À terme, Farakan Labs prévoit d'élargir l'offre de PengMe à d'autres solutions de financement d'urgence destinées aux particuliers, aux micro-entreprises et aux PME. Les promoteurs envisagent notamment des produits liés au financement du fonds de roulement, des bons de commande, de l'affacturage ou encore des services d'assurance, en partenariat avec des institutions financières agréées. Pour Jérôme Kaboré, le projet est né du constat que de nombreux salariés, commerçants, micro-entrepreneurs et dirigeants de PME disposent d'activités rentables, mais peinent à obtenir rapidement des ressources financières lorsqu'un besoin urgent survient, notamment en dehors des horaires d'ouverture des banques. Avec PengMe, Farakan Labs entend ainsi accélérer la digitalisation des services financiers d'urgence au Burkina Faso. En jouant le rôle d'interface entre les utilisateurs, les entreprises et les institutions financières, la startup ambitionne de rendre l'accès à des financements rapides plus simple, plus sécurisé et mieux adapté aux réalités du quotidien des travailleurs et des entrepreneurs. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Farakan Labs lance PengMe, une plateforme pour faciliter l'avance sur salaire en cas d'urgence est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .
